title: Environmental, Social, and Governance (Esg) Reporting and Capital Market Response in Africa: A Systematic Review of Literature
abstract: Purpose: The paper focused on all-inclusive mixture of old and current qualitative and quantitative literature on the link between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting and capital market response in the style of ESG reporting to meet global standard. However, most African quoted companies have not indoctrinated ESG reporting style in their day-to-day financial and non-financial reporting due to lack of adoption of sustainability practices which make most companies in Africa not survive economic crisis and fail to attract foreign capital market investors. The paper systematically reviewed the link between ESG reporting and capital market response.  Design/Methodology/Approach: Both qualitative and empirical evidences were amassed over the period of 2004-2025 but papers started download from year 2012-2025 as started by Scopus database, this insinuates no paper published in the Scopus database between 2004-2011. This period of 2004-2011, ESG reporting had not come to limelight style of reporting among quoted companies’ activities. The study reviewed 73 articles downloaded from Scopus database within the period of 2004-2025 through PRISMA guidelines.  Findings: The review revealed that outside Africa context, the firm that full adopted ESG reporting enhance sustainability practices and attract domestic and foreign capital market investors which in turn improve firms’ contribution to green economic activities.  Implication/Originality/Value: The systematic review indicates that ESG reporting by quoted companies create good and bad news response and companies that embrace ESG reporting improve sustainability practices which attract foreign capital market investors and such companies survive economic crisis. Despite global push by United Nation on sustainability practices and adoption, firms in Africa still face ESG reporting gap which hinder sustainability reporting quality of firms in developing countries like Africa. Thus, Government and capital market regulators should make it compulsory that before firm could be listed in the capital market and get license for operations in Africa, sustainability practices and sustainable development goals agenda must be embrace and consented to by firms as well as adopt ESG reporting framework which will enhance sustainable growth in Africa.
venue_name: Journal of Accounting and Finance in Emerging Economies, Vol 12, Iss 1 (2026)

title: Exercise-Based Interventions Combined with Branched-Chain Amino Acid Supplementation for the Prevention and Management of Sarcopenia in Liver Cirrhosis: A Scoping Review
abstract: Sarcopenia is a common and clinically relevant complication of liver cirrhosis, associated with impaired physical function, reduced quality of life (QOL) , and increased morbidity and mortality. Various nutritional and exercise strategies, including branched-chain ami-no acid (BCAA) supplementation, have been proposed to mitigate muscle loss; however, evidence on their combined effects remains heterogeneous. This review aimed to map the existing evidence on the effects of physical activity combined with BCAA supplementa-tion on muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance in patients with liver cirrhosis. A scoping review was conducted to map the available evidence on structured exercise interventions combined with BCAA supplementation in adults with liver cirrho-sis. Electronic searches were performed in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to identify relevant studies reporting muscle related or functional outcomes. Data were charted and synthesized narratively to describe intervention characteristics, outcome measures, and overall trends in the literature. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Inter-ventions consisted mainly of walking-based exercise or combined aerobic and resistance training programs lasting 8–12 weeks, along with oral BCAA supplementation. Physical activity was consistently associated with improvements in muscle strength, physical performance, or frailty-related outcomes, while effects on muscle mass were more variable. Exercise based rehabilitation appears to be a central component in the management of sarcopenia in liver cirrhosis. BCAA supplementation may provide supportive benefits when combined with physical activity; however, its independent effects remain incon-sistent

title: Association of computed tomography–based morphological parameters with rupture status in middle cerebral artery aneurysms: a retrospective case series and literature review
abstract: Unruptured intracranial aneurysms are increasingly diagnosed due to the widespread use of noninvasive imaging modalities in clinical practice. Hemodynamic stress is considered an important factor in aneurysm formation and rupture, and both aneurysm geometry and surrounding vascular morphology have been reported to be associated with rupture status in the literature. Middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysms account for approximately 35% of intracranial aneurysms and are frequently implicated in subarachnoid hemorrhage. In this retrospective single-center case series, we evaluated computed tomography–based morphological parameters in eight patients with MCA aneurysms (four ruptured and four unruptured). Descriptive comparisons were performed to explore potential differences between groups. Additionally, a structured literature review was conducted to contextualize our findings within previously reported morphological factors associated with rupture status. Although several size- and angle-related parameters demonstrated directional differences between ruptured and unruptured aneurysms, no statistically significant associations were identified. Given the limited sample size, the findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Accurate assessment of rupture risk remains a major clinical challenge. Larger prospective, multi-center studies integrating advanced imaging analysis are required to validate morphological markers and to better inform individualized treatment decisions

title: Révéler l’invisible. Le rôle de trois artistes africaines-américaines dans la visibilité de leur communauté au xxe siècle
abstract: Cette étude analyse le rôle essentiel de trois artistes africaines-américaines – Augusta Savage (1892-1962), Faith Ringgold (1930-2024) et Ming Smith (née en 1950) – dans le processus artistique de visibilisation de leur communauté. Leur travail à travers trois médiums différents (sculpture, peinture et photographie) a permis de révéler des réalités ignorées par la société américaine en luttant contre l’invisibilité sociale des Africains-Américains.Gamin (1929) de Savage et Black Light Series (1967-1969) de Ringgold ont célébré la beauté noire en offrant, par le visage, une réponse à la déshumanisation souvent imposée aux Africains-Américains. De son côté, la série Invisible Man (1988-1991) et America Seen Through Stars and Stripes (1997) de Smith représentent la complexité de l’identité noire à travers des œuvres qui explorent la notion d’effacement dans un contexte urbain.Au-delà de la visibilisation d’individus, ces artistes ont réinventé le récit national américain en y intégrant l’expérience africaine-américaine, que ce soit par les bustes de leaders noirs de Savage, les quilts narratifs de Ringgold ou les portraits de personnalités noires influentes de Smith.En confrontant les stéréotypes raciaux, en dénonçant les injustices et en affirmant la valeur de la culture noire au sein du canon artistique américain, ces trois femmes ont fait plus qu’utiliser leur travail comme un outil d’engagement social et politique, elles ont également mené des actions militantes personnelles.

title: La réception des Pensées de Pascal au Japon : Miki Kiyoshi lecteur du « pari »
abstract: This article examines the reception in Japan of Blaise Pascal’s famous “wager” through the interpretation proposed by the philosopher Miki Kiyoshi (1897-1945). While Pascal was initially read in Japan mainly within a religious context, Miki was the first to introduce his work into the field of philosophy proper. Influenced by Heidegger as well as by the Buddhist tradition of Jōdo Shinshū, Miki developed an original existential and religious interpretation of the Pensées, focusing in particular on Pascal’s wager. This article first reconstructs Miki’s intellectual and biographical background, emphasizing his reflections on death, anxiety, and contingency as fundamental dimensions of human existence. It then examines his engagement with Jules Lachelier’s critique of the wager, which rejected its purely mathematical interpretation and instead understood it as a practical and existential act involving the subject’s transformation. Finally, this article shows how Miki reinterprets the wager as an existential transition grounded in what he calls “religious anxiety”. For Miki, the wager is not a logical proof of the existence of God but an act of the will through which the finite subject confronts its own finitude and opens itself to the infinite. In this way, the wager becomes a fundamental structure of human experience, in which anxiety is transformed into hope.
publisher: Groupe de Recherches Interdisciplinaires sur l'Histoire du Littéraire

title: Les singes de Pascal : politique du style autour de Port-Royal
abstract: Regardless of his philosophical and theological thought, Pascal appeared to authors of the second half of the 17th century as an essential reference point for satirical style. Thus, beyond a purely stylistic analysis of the Provincial Letters, this article aims to demonstrate that Pascal’s style served as a benchmark from the 1660s onward, used to legitimize or delegitimize satirical texts of the period. A comparative study of Racine’s letters against Nicole’s Imaginaires and Boileau’s Epistle XII on the Love of God reveals various uses of Pascal’s style, which then emerges as a polemical tool capable of triggering further polemics. Leaving aside any specific imitable stylistic facts, Pascal’s style thus appears to be a pure signature, that is, a literary category available to rival authors seeking to replicate the impact of the Provincial Letters.

title: Le Pascal de Paul Bourget
abstract: This article examines Blaise Pascal’s philosophical and spiritual influence on Paul Bourget’s work and thought. It first shows how Bourget, drawing on Pascal’s notion of the disproportion of man, seeks to overcome modern pessimism and scientific monism. Pascal thus plays a major role in the development of a moral psychology open to faith. Finally, the article sheds light on the public and ideological reappropriation of Pascal in Bourget’s literary consecration.

title: Pouvoir, neutralisation et « non-reproduction » dans Les Trois discours sur la condition des grands
abstract: The work Trois discours sur la condition des grands testifies to an ethics of self-knowledge that lays bare the truth concerning the foundation of the prince’s sovereignty. From the perspective of Louis Marin, this text –whose attribution to Blaise Pascal remains doubtful– develops a critique of absolutism that reveals the neutralizing effects immanent in power. By foregrounding a specific political function of negation, this article therefore aims to emphasize both the affinities and the divergences between Marin’s commentary, on the one hand, and, on the other, the analysis developed by Chantal Jaquet in her book Les Transclasses ou la non-reproduction. The expression “non-reproduction,” through the negation it contains, thus illustrates a utopian instance which, far from identifying as a meritocratic ideology, highlights the contradictions inherent in the enunciation of the identity. The expression refers to an infinite movement of differentiation that deconstructs the ontological status of the political subject.

title: Écrire je
abstract: This article focuses on statements in the first person found in some of the books containing Pascal’s Pensées. Its aim is to use these statements as a starting point to contribute to the discussion about “how to do things with words” and, more specifically, to the debate on how this concept can be applied in historical analysis. The condition of the papers found upon Pascal’s death makes it impossible to seriously attempt to characterize the action that Pascal as an individual might have undertaken with the words written on these papers, which became the Pensées. In other words, it is illusory to speculate about an action other than the choice of these written words itself, other than this work that left fragments capable of all sorts of external interpretations of coherence. The Pensées exist, however, because Pascal’s contemporaries set about constructing their coherence: the fact that the distinction between the work of writing—the act of choosing words on paper—and the actions carried out with the writings that result from it has, in this instance, been preserved for us is part of the book’s critical strength. To outline the implications of this configuration, the presence of the first-person singular in the excerpts studied serves as a guide in the article.

title: Les libraires-imprimeurs « jansénistes » existent-ils ?
abstract: This study examines the so‑called “Jansenist” printer‑booksellers involved in the publication of Les Provinciales. Louis Batiffol first analysed their position and participation in the polemics surrounding the Petites Lettres, while Henri‑Jean Martin, founder of the history of the book, later shed further light on the case of the bookseller Guillaume Desprez, known for his collaboration with Jansenist circles.Building on these two modern studies, this paper aims to identify and clarify the names and roles of the printer‑booksellers involved in the printing of the Lettres, following the chronology of their production. The organisational structure that emerges from this examination proves to be particularly striking.The label “Jansenist” is frequently—and often without explicit justification—applied not only to writers such as Arnauld, Nicole, and Pascal, but also to printer‑booksellers, as if they all shared identical doctrinal commitments. Yet the grounds on which these publishers may be described by this epithet remain unclear. Among the cases discussed, that of Ballard, syndic of the community of printer‑booksellers between 1652 and 1657, is especially revealing. His case illustrates the ambiguity of the term “Jansenist” and demonstrates that relationships between these professionals and Jansenist authors were not necessarily based on ideological adherence or loyalty.

title: National Cuisines à la Carte. The Hierarchies and Circulation of National Cuisines in the Field of Transnational Gastronomy
abstract: This article examines the structure, hierarchies, and circulation of “national cuisines” in the field of transnational gastronomy through a dual empirical entry point: the restaurant selection in 28 European capitals and the circulation of the twelve most widespread “national cuisines.” Principal component analysis reveals the dual structure of the field: a restricted-circulation pole, dominated by expert hierarchies, and a mainstream pole, in which success for a cuisine is defined by its degree of diffusion. The regularities identified in the circulation of certain national cuisines demonstrate the validity of the transnational approach proposed, revealing different diffusion models. This research highlights the importance of studying the circulation of national cuisines in their reciprocal relationships and across different price ranges, showing how the symbolic value linked to a national origin has strong performative power in the European restaurant market.

title: Processus critiques, idées et causalité. Entretien avec Michel Dobry
abstract: Renowned for his seminal work on the sociology of political crises, Michel Dobry seems, at first glance, to have only a distant connection to the history of ideas. Indeed, his approach might even suggest that the role of beliefs and ideas is secondary in the analysis of the political change. Yet his research is among those that have significantly influenced the renewal of social history of political ideas these last decades. This interview with Michel Dobry is focused on this paradox. It explores Dobry’s relationship with (social) history of political ideas, notably with its main authors like Zeev Sternhell and Quentin Skinner, but also with the debates surrounding the category of “fascism” and the problem of defining categories, the question of legitimacy in the maintenance of social order, and, more broadly, that of the social effectiveness of ideas.

title: When the Masculine Elite is at the Table: Reproducing Class and Gender Hierarchies through Gastronomy within a Parisian High Society Club
abstract: This article studies the symbolic and social dimensions of elite gastronomy as an instrument of social distinction that legitimizes domination. My analysis focuses on the Club des Cent, a private members’ dining club which was founded in Paris in 1912 and is only open to men. The club meets every Thursday lunchtime at a Paris restaurant for a meal organized by one of its members. This article draws on fieldwork, including interviews, and the archives of club members and newspapers to analyse the gastronomic discourses and practices of the elites. In doing so, it shows how French gastronomy is used to reinforce class and gender hierarchies.

title: Faire de la traduction des sciences sociales un métier. Autonomisation et professionnalisation des traductrices spécialisées
abstract: This article examines the process of professionalization and autonomization of translation in the field of humanities and social sciences (HSS). This contribution is the result of a qualitative study based on interviews with professional translators specialised in HSS. The study is completed by observation, facilitated by the author’s professional position—as editorial assistant of HSS journals. A first part is about the low level of recognition of the HSS translation as an autonomous sector, both within the research community and regarding the other translation specialities. Academics, because of their specific internationalization strategies and the lack of funding, often bypass professional translation to favour self-translation or peer-translation. Between art and expertise, “literary” and “technical” translation, the HSS sector receives marginal attention from professional organizations dedicated to representing translators or scientific editors. Major technological innovations (neural machine translation and generative artificial intelligence) are intrinsically linked to organizational changes (notably the growth of translation agencies). Thus, digital transition highlights a low level of professional recognition which is an incentive for specialised translators—in particular the most qualified segment—to organize for the defense of their professional territory.

title: Towards a “Non-Violent” Kitchen? Violence and the Anti-Violence Discourse in French Fine Dining Kitchens
abstract: The aim of this article is to demonstrate that advocating for a fight against violence within fine dining in France can be analysed as an attempt at a symbolic revolution in the field of fine dining. As a starting point, this article examines the forms taken by violence in this sector and the various reactions elicited in relation to cooks’ dispositions, resources, and career paths, in order to show that this advocacy occurs on the margins of the occupation.

title: Une production symbolique du capitalisme responsable : le cas de l’huile de palme durable
abstract: This article examines so-called sustainable foods as a symbolic production of responsible capitalism. It focuses on the controversy surrounding the proposed taxation of palm oil in France between 2012 and 2016 (the “Nutella tax”). Initially introduced on political and public health grounds, the tax was gradually abandoned as a new narrative of “sustainable” palm oil took hold. Drawing on an analysis of parliamentary debates, communications from public and private actors, and a media corpus, the article shows how corporate lobbying and communication strategies redirected the issues at stake, turning a public health priority into a matter of sustainable development. Framing companies as competing for salvation rather than for profit enabled agri-food industries to continue their economic activity within a form of salvation capitalism, cast as serving the common good.

title: Étudier la fabrique des biens symboliques alimentaires
abstract: Cooking as an activity of symbolic production is rarely addressed in the social science literature, which is surprising considering the great diversity of its transformations, from the inspired distinction of artistic cuisine to everyday domestic practices and the mass production of the food industry. The contributions to this issue approach cooking from a variety of angles. The subject of professional labour is central, with papers on home chefs (S. Naulin) and workplace violence in fine-dining restaurants (A. Hacot), and the place of cooking in the broader economy of domestic labour. The symbolic and distinctive power of cooking is highlighted in papers on the social image of the culinary activity and depiction as an art (A. Pégourdie) and on a Parisian men-only society club that uses fine dining as a pretext for an elite male sociability (M. Lassery). Questions surrounding the production of culture through the circulation of “national cuisines” in the restaurants of European capitals are also examined in an article (A. De Silva). Lastly, this issue also considers the agri-business, industrial food sector in an article on palm oil as a political and economic object (T. Depecker).

Initially introduced on political and public health grounds, the tax was gradually abandoned as a new narrative of “sustainable” palm oil took hold. Drawing on an analysis of parliamentary debates, communications from public and private actors, and a media corpus, the article shows how corporate lobbying and communication strategies redirected the issues at stake, turning a public health priority into a matter of sustainable development. Framing companies as competing for salvation rather than for profit enabled agri-food industries to continue their economic activity within a form of salvation capitalism, cast as serving the common good.

title: Being Your Own Chef. Are Digital Platforms a Professional Emancipation Vehicle for Expert Service Workers?
abstract: This article examines the extent to which digital platforms are a professional emancipation vehicle for expert service workers providing personalized services. It focuses on the case of a personal chef platform to investigate its emancipatory effect for cooks seeking to escape the constraints of waged employment in the food service industry and entrepreneurship as a restaurateur. Drawing on interviews with twelve cooks and a platform manager as well as web scraping of the 283 chef profiles on the platform, the study analyses three aspects of emancipation: economic autonomy, existential autonomy (consisting of rethinking the place of work in life) and autonomy in the exercise of the work itself. The article shows that emancipation is incomplete. Earnings remain low, professional constraints are more reconfigured than eliminated, and new forms of subjection to customers and the platform can emerge.

title: Devenir son propre chef. Les plateformes numériques permettent-elles l’émancipation professionnelle des travailleurs experts des services ?

title: Organisation du travail culinaire et consommation de produits ultratransformés
abstract: In both expert and lay discourse, home cooking is seen as a rampart against unhealthy eating, as epitomized by ultraprocessed “industrial” foods. Culinary discourse of this kind contributes to the creation of symbolic frontiers of class and gender. In this article, we test the assumption upon which this discourse is based, i.e. that more time spent in the kitchen, by women in particular, is associated with lower ultraprocessed food consumption. Drawing on INSEE’s 2017 Household Budget survey (enquête Budget de famille), we focus on a sample of 3,210 couple households and use the NOVA nutritional definition of ultraprocessed foods. Our findings run counter to received ideas. Couples with the lowest incomes or educational levels are not the largest consumers of these products, and spending on ultraprocessed foods does not decrease when couples eat more home-cooked meals. While the youngest couples spend more on these foods, households with children, identified in the literature as the most receptive to messaging about healthy eating, are also large ultraprocessed food consumers.

title: Cooking and Art: A Field of Cultural Production under the Influence of the Market
abstract: This article addresses the relationship between professional culinary excellence and art. Whilst in existing scholarship philosophical approaches suppose an ontological link between these two categories and sociological research employs the concept of “artification,” my analysis is based on field theory. I consider cooking as a field of cultural production, which allows for the constructivist approach behind the legitimization of cooking to be translated through making use of the artistic comparison. The first part of the article demonstrates the extent to which cooking assumes the properties of fields of cultural production: a specific concern and a vocation discourse to succeed, recognition authorities led by peers and critics, a dynamic of disputes between avant-garde and consecrated chefs against the backdrop of permanent revolution. The second part addresses the specificities of the culinary field and, in particular, its lack of autonomy from the economic domain. This assessment leads to a broader reflection on the principles of distance between artistic fields and the market, in which I also interrogate the underlying principles of an economy of disinterestedness.

title: Uses of Raewyn Connell in the Construction of the Sub-Field of Masculinities Studies in France: The HSS Scholar as a Symbolic Good
abstract: By understanding the HSS (humanities and social sciences) scholar as a symbolic good, this article shows the intertwining of the French reception of the sociology of Raewyn Connell—an internationally leading figure in masculinities studies—and of the construction of a sub-field of masculinities studies in France. Drawing on his PhD research, the author evidences a significant increase in references to Connell’s work in French HSS scholarship and a spike of translations into French at the turn of the 2010s. This was the work of young scholars, based at EHESS, who saw Connell as a symbolic good that they used to confer legitimacy on their own research and contribute to the institutionalization of their research themes.

title: Usages de Raewyn Connell dans la formation du sous-champ des études sur les masculinités en France. L’autrice de SHS comme bien symbolique

title: La peau d’un agneau innocent. Jack Cade, la voix, la loi et l’écrit
abstract: “Is not a lamentable thing, that of the skin of an innocent Lambe should be made Parchment ; that Parchement being scribeld ore, should undoe a man.” These words spoken by Jack Cade in Shakespeare’s Henry VI, Part II form the starting point of this study devoted to the textual genealogy and possible interpretations by audiences and readers of several of Cade’s lines : “Away ! Burn all the records of the realm. My mouth shall be the Parliament of England,” or “our forefathers had no other books but the score and the tally.” Analysing Cade’s language, which is imbued with biblical quotations and legal traditions, and by examining the multiple manifestations of the materiality of written culture within the play, this study seeks to understand the enigmatic, paradoxical and unstable portrayal the play offers of the rebellion led by Jack Cade and the Kentish artisans in 1450. The playwright or playwrights (Shakespeare and Marlowe ? Peele ? Greene ?) have interwoven lexicons, brought eras into collision, and attributed to a framed and insignificant character the very words of egalitarian revolts. It is these ambiguities and contradictions that explain the critical disagreements regarding the meaning of these scenes, as well as their diverse and contradictory theatrical stagings.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Les fausses approbations de censure au XVIIIe siècle : pistes de réflexion sur des marges parodiques
abstract: From 1701 until the French Revolution, any work published through legal channels was required to be reviewed by a royal censor. This review was explicitly indicated by the presence of an “approval” in the paratext. This text, combining set formulas with a space for free expression, became an easy target for parody. Throughout the century, some authors inserted fake approvals in the margins of their works, mimicking official certificates while subverting them. These forged endorsements provide valuable insight into how censorship was perceived and received by writers and readers alike, through their layout choices, use of humour, and the invention of fictitious censors.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: “In my wood to dwell”: Margaret Cavendish’s Ecocritical Thinking and her Uses of Allegory in Poetry
abstract: Margaret Cavendish is now routinely enrolled as an early example of an eco-conscious author, and studied through the perspective lens of ecocritical approaches, but the risk of anachronism is strong. Her ecocriticism needs to be reassessed in light of her philosophical conception of nature. This article aims at contextualising her professed concern for the natural world in relation to the literary tradition of prosopopeias of trees, seventeenth-century politics and her philosophical conception of nature, looking in particular at one of her 1653 dialogues, a long poem of 164 lines in rhymed pentameters entitled “A Dialogue between an Oak and a Man Cutting Him Down”. This poem, which includes the tree’s plea to the feller not to be hacked, has comfortably been read in recent critical studies in an ecocritical perspective. Yet the convention of the tree prosopopeia, which goes back to the Bible and Ovid, had already been used by Drayton, among others, in his popular Poly-Olbion (1619). Placing Cavendish’s approach within this tradition allows us to better understand the articulation between her genuine concern for the natural world, political allegory and her natural philosophy. Focusing on Cavendish’s complex allegorical technique in the poem, this article studies her discursive uses of the oak as a multifaceted emblem, which requires hermeneutic agility on the part of the readers – and proves once more, if need be, that her poetry is more sophisticated than was once thought.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Thinking with Trees: Philosophical and Legal Genealogies in “Auto-Icon” and Other Texts by Jeremy Bentham (1748-1832)
abstract: This article focuses on a late, unfinished and unpublished treatise by Jeremy Bentham entitled “Auto-Icon; or, Farther Uses of the Dead to the Living”, in which the tree of knowledge, the tree of law (arbor jurisdictionis) and the genealogical tree are interwoven. The Auto-Icons – or effigies – of philosophers and legal theorists were to be brought in conversation, comparing their positions on topics such as learning, law and legacies. On epistemological matters, Bentham sought to correct the failings of earlier models of tree diagrams, but remained convinced that the tree was the best model to offer an overview of the structure of arts and sciences. The tree proved as much a resource as a challenge, raising questions about its composition, orientation, ornamentation, as well as the desirable number of subdivisions. Answering such questions led Bentham to position himself in a genealogy of philosophers. But the tree is also very much present in the discussion of the “commemorational” uses to which Auto-Icons could be put, not least because woods and trees played a key role in the construction of the Common Law tradition as an unbroken patrilinear genealogy. Through the use of irony and satire, Bentham seems to mock both the pretensions of the nobility and, in a reflective gesture, his own bid for posthumous fame. With its excesses and oddities, “Auto-Icon” reminds readers that the tree is not a “natural” metaphor and that its various uses have a history, which needs to be traced so as to contextualize the ideology such uses convey.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Trees in William Cowper’s Poetry
abstract: This article tackles how William Cowper (1731-1800) uses trees in The Task (1783-1784), “The Poplar Field” (1783-1784?), and “Yardley Oak,” an unfinished poem from 1791, as figures of the expressive and the emblematical. The British poet has recourse to a set of artistic traits, borrowing from pictorial, architectural and musical techniques to make trees a fulcrum of his landscape descriptions. The interplay of colours, as well as light and shade, are two of the techniques he uses to capture variations in tones and shapes, while expressing his admiration for the beauty of trees. Yet that does not prevent him from lamenting the transformation of the landscape he dearly loves as a result of human intervention – the felling of poplars being the most obvious example –, in addition to the growing distance between trees and people, who no longer take advantage of the shade the former give. Besides, trees exemplify Cowper’s reflection about what time and human life stand for, giving him the opportunity to steer his poems in a meditative direction: the oak and poplar, to which he devoted specific texts, reflect the poet’s condition, and are furthermore a mirror of human frailty and mortality, as reflected in his analogy between the human body and a tree’s branches and trunk, which both grow before declining.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: La critique de l’ethnocentrisme dans les Nouveaux Mémoires sur l’état présent de la Chine de Louis Le Comte (1696)
abstract: Back in France, Jesuit missionary Louis Le Comte published his Nouveaux Mémoires sur l’état présent de la Chine in 1696. His admiring remarks on the religion of the ancient Chinese caused such a scandal that the Sorbonne censored the work in 1700. In the Nouveaux Mémoires, Le Comte undertakes a critique of ethnocentrism, initially directed at the collective “vanity” of the Chinese, then subtly turned against France itself. In his view, both China and France display flaws worthy of condemnation or ridicule – and even certain barbaric traits – that call into question their claims to superiority. This article explores the mechanisms of this critique of ethnocentrism, which invites reflection on the relativity of customs. It also highlights the limits of this discourse – most notably Le Comte’s Christian-centric perspective, which sometimes leads him to deny Chinese alterity, for instance by portraying Confucius as a herald of the Messiah and China as a nation unconsciously shaped by Christianity.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: The Tree that Hides the Man: The Use and Misuse of Arboreal Symbols in Thomas of Woodstock (c. 1591-1595)
abstract: “The huge greate Oke was once a plant.” This observation, found in Timothy Kendall’s anthology Flower of epigrammes (1577), seems to state the obvious: trees do grow from smaller (and frailer) plants and are subject to time. Yet this contrasts with the emblematic oak of early modern poetry and political theory – a symbol of strength, immutability, and royal majesty. As Andrew McRae (2012) notes, however, “the politics of the oak – and of trees more generally” – were not as settled in the sixteenth century as they would become later, thus paving the way for all sorts of rhetorical play. Focusing on the anonymous play Thomas of Woodstock (c. 1591-1595), this article explores how such arboreal symbols as the oak were manipulated and subverted on stage. This article argues that the play, in interrogating the use and misuse of trees – both as rhetorical tropes and as concrete natural elements – subtly challenges core tenets of royal orthodoxy. It questions the merging of the king’s two bodies and undermines the king’s uniqueness, thereby unveiling the fragility of symbols meant to uphold royal authority.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Fairy-Thinking and the Labyrinth: The Forest Palimpsest in Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595)
abstract: In Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595), the forest outside Athens functions as an alternative space to the courtly world of supposed order and the rule of law. Constructed as a palimpsest of various layers, the forest is multi-faceted with shifting guises and roles. As a mirror to the court, it reflects government in a different form; and, as part of an ecology in crisis, it resonates with the flawed leadership and failed nurturing of patriarchal Athenian society. Maze-like and a place of wonder, the forest of A Midsummer Night’s Dream is both enchanting and threatening, as the motif of the labyrinth, with the Theseus and Minotaur intertext, haunts the forest. It is also a creative blank space, where desires and fears can be projected and encountered, offering a place to perform and rehearse the potential for tragedy and transformation. In the play, the fairies and the forest are closely aligned, both leading mortals astray and literalising the journey of the psyche through the labyrinth. This article argues that the interlinked fairies and forest are key to the play’s imaginary, and that their overlapping mythic intertexts enable thinking through human flaws and nurturing responsibilities. I conceptualise this as fairy-thinking, the projecting of the human into a magical green space. Through fairy-thinking, humans confront the other within themselves in negotiating the arboreal labyrinth and moving towards renewal.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: The Trees of the Muses in Aemilia Lanyer’s “The Description of Cooke-ham” (1611)
abstract: This essay analyses the symbolism of trees in Aemilia Lanyer’s poem “The Description of Cooke-ham” (1611) to highlight her mnemonic, protofeminist reconstruction of nature. Contrary to what other critics have suggested, the poem’s evocation of nature cannot be reduced to an early example of what John Ruskin called “pathetic fallacy”. While nature is presenting as feeling, it is not solely the projection of the persona’s emotions that are being expressed. The anthropomorphisation of trees acknowledges the alterity of nature as the speaker strives to offer an interpretation that does resonate with her own feelings as she leaves the estate. Their distinctive species and characteristics take on symbolic meanings that tie “The Description of Cooke-ham” to the long religious poem to which it was appended, Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum. Moreover, the references to Philomela and Echo – two myths that connect women’s experiences and nature – signal Lanyer’s poetic attempt to recover the valley of the Muses of Greek mythology by displacing it into an English pastoral context. More than landmarks that illustrate the poem’s topographical function, the trees of Cooke-ham are essential to Lanyer’s poetics by connecting the natural and the female in their commonality.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Of Trees, Harps and Lutes
abstract: The intricate relationship between music, instruments, and trees in Elizabethan England is explored through an analysis of various literary and pedagogical texts of the period. While the connection between trees and music is often overlooked in early modern English discourse, it is found to be deeply embedded in the symbolic representations of musicians and archetypal musical scenes. This article delves into the materiality of musical instruments, discussing the types of wood used and their symbolic associations. In this light, the mythical stories of Orpheus and Apollo are then examined, highlighting the magical and transformative power of music over nature, as well as the physical and emotional resonance between musicians and their instruments. Through an exploration of poetry, prose, and historical accounts, this study sheds light on the significance of wood in the creation and performance of music, revealing a complex interplay between art, nature, and human intervention.

title: Reading the Early Modern Energy Crisis through Shakespeare: A Cultural History of Coal
abstract: This article draws attention to an overlooked phenomenon both in the history of early modern England and in the Shakespearean canon, namely coal and charcoal production at the turn of the seventeenth century. In early use, coal, which is duly mentioned in Shakespeare’s plays and poems, denoted mineral coal as well as charcoal but, in most cases, the playwright uses “coal” as synonymous with “charcoal”. This leads to two questions: why did the playwright seemingly promote charcoal over sea-coal at a time when the pollution resulting from domestic and industrial coal smoke was becoming perceptible? And what does this reality tell us about the early modern perspective on energy during a period of wood shortage? In order to address such questions, I would like to determine what can be more specifically learnt from the representation of charcoal – linked to wood felling and deforestation – in Shakespeare’s works: I pay attention not only to what he says about it, but also to what he does with it. I first turn to the plays in order to understand how they adumbrate a number of economic issues correlated to the use of charcoal, notably by dwelling on the figure of the collier with a series of puns exchanged by Sampson and Gregory in the opening scene of Romeo and Juliet, as well as on the early modern war industry, whose links with the theatre, which required canons, gunpowder and fireworks for its spectacular effects, are often underestimated. I then examine how Shakespeare refers to the production of charcoal in an era of severe environmental crisis. In this period marked by the depletion of English forests, the felling of wood for charcoal was particularly frowned upon, so that new strategies emerged, and coppicing, a technique mentioned in Love’s Labour’s Lost, became an alternative means of producing charcoal without infringing the law. Such economic and material considerations should not make us forget, however, the important role assigned to charcoal in aesthetic and cosmetic terms: the playwright must have been aware of its potentialities, and while he seems to reveal, in The Rape of Lucrece, a genuine familiarity with the techniques of painting, he also refers to the charcoal make-up of the actors playing Aaron, in Titus Andronicus, or Othello, in the tragedy of the same name. My chief objective here is to trace a number of silent connections between past and present and to engage in an ecocritical and aesthetic reflection on Shakespeare’s representation of the uses and misuses of energy.
concepts: French literature - Italian literature - Spanish literature - Portuguese literature

title: Désarmement démographique. De l’écologie politique au féminisme, la grève des naissances contre le nucléaire
abstract: In the spring of 1979, women and men protesting the construction of a nuclear power plant in Tarn-et-Garonne declared they would not give birth anymore until the French government abandoned its civilian and military nuclear policy. The idea was immediately taken up by environmentalist women in Lower Saxony and soon took root within the West German feminist movement. This article seeks to understand the political and semantic transformation of the birth strike as it was appropriated by activists and as it spread geographically. It analyses how different groups, in the end of a decade marked by feminist struggles for women’s freedom to gain power over their own bodies, politicized issues of procreation and motherhood.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: « D’ennemis à amis » : appropriations des relations franco-allemandes et mises en récit de soi par les « Malgré-Nous »
abstract: This article examines how individuals, at the most intimate and private level, appropriate international policies to construct a narrative of their past. It shows that social position, gender and associative or partisan commitments influence both the selection of Franco-German policies and the resulting reinterpretation of the past. Drawing on the testimony of a « Malgré-Nous », forcibly conscripted into the Wehrmacht, the article reveals how Franco-German reconciliation policies retrospectively shape these witnesses accounts of their friendly relations with German soldiers they met during the Second World War and their gender performances.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Demokratiebildender Geschichtsunterricht im 21. Jahrhundert – Zwischen esprit critique und Geschichtsbewusstsein
abstract: This article takes the Franco-Prussian War of 1870/71 and its aftermath as a case study to compare the culture of tasks and questions in German and French upper-secondary history textbooks. It focuses on how two central categories in history education – historical consciousness in Germany and esprit critique in France – shape students’ engagement with sources, either by encouraging normatively evaluative judgments or by encouraging questions oriented towards historical explanation. Drawing on Marc Bloch’s understanding-oriented conception of history and a scholarly approach inspired by historical thinking, the article opens a discussion on the conditions under which history teaching can contribute to democratic education in the twenty-first century.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Medialität, Fiktion und Autorschaft im autobiographischen schreiben des digitalen Zeitalters: eine Analyse von Wolfgang Herrndorfs Arbeit und Struktur und Éric Chevillards L’autofictif
abstract: This article explores the evolution of autobiographical writing in the digital age through a close reading of Wolfgang Herrndorf’s Arbeit und Struktur and Éric Chevillard’s L’Autofictif – blogs later published as books. These hybrid forms provide a lens for examining how technological mediation shapes subjectivity and blurs the boundaries between reality and fiction. The tension between blog and book as media further raises critical questions about the evolving definition of literature itself. Autofiction and automediality serve as productive frameworks for analysing these texts, foregrounding the ways in which digital environments reconfigure self-representation. The texts construct a deliberate authorial stance, which draws attention to the performative dimensions of selfhood intensified by the virtual.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: L’éducation esthétique comme émancipation dans l’œuvre de Peter Weiss, au prisme de la pensée de Jacques Rancière
abstract: After he narrated his way out of an authoritarian education, Peter Weiss focused his Aesthetics of Resistance around the educational processes of young workers through the experience of mainly visual artworks. In this novel, Weiss rewrote the project of an “aesthetic education” for the purposes of emancipation of the dominated groups. This novel echoes some of the main themes of Jacques Rancière’s thought. This essay aims at rereading Peter Weiss’s novel under the lens of Rancière’s philosophy; through a polyphonic writing that mixes reflection and narration, this work tries to interrupt the “distribution of the sensible” (Rancière).
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Germaine de Staël et la métamorphose de Faust I
abstract: The first introduction of Faust I (1808) to French readers, presented by Germaine de Staël in De l’Allemagne (1813), takes the form of an unfaithful translation. This infidelity seems to contradict both the aesthetic orientation of the work and the translation principles Staël herself advocates. Drawing on the perspective of cultural transfer, this article explores the motivations behind this rewriting. It argues that Staël reshapes Goethe’s text in order to mediate between French and German aesthetic traditions, addressing differences in dramatic taste, the poetic capacities of language, and the role attributed to imagination.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Asterix übersetzen: kulturelle Adaption eines popkulturellen Werks
abstract: Pop-cultural works such as comics are cultural artefacts that bear witness to their time and usually reflect the contemporary context in which they were created. This article uses the example of the French comic book series Asterix by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo to examine elements and their representation of the political, historical and socio-cultural context, as well as the design and production-related decisions that have made the work a pop culture phenomenon since the late 1950s. As examples, several allusions and representations of this context of origin are identified at the image and text level of the comics. Also, Gudrun Penndorf’s translation decisions in the standard German versions are examined. In addition to the question of the adaptability of cultural phenomena, special attention is paid to the influence of the German reception context and the question of the formation of a common European culture.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Literarische Darstellungen anthropologischer Transformationen: der Übergang von galanten zu empfindsamen Liebesdiskursen
abstract: Starting from a moral theory from Thomasius, this article addresses the discontinuity of literary representations of morality and love in the 18th century with Enlightenment narratives, such as the rationalization of emotions. Using discourses as statement-contexts, it is shown that in gallant texts (17th/18th century) the discourse of rational love is at the center, while in sentimental texts (18th/19th century) the discourse of unreasonable love takes that central place. Hunold's Die liebenswürdige Adalie, La Roche's Geschichte des Fräuleins von Sternheim, and Goethe's Die Leiden des jungen Werthers in the 1774 version are examined.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Le rôle de la frontière dans l’adaptation au changement climatique des agriculteur.ice.s du Rhin Supérieur (France, Allemagne, Suisse)
abstract: The Upper Rhine is a coherent cross-border region shared between France, Germany, and Switzerland. Cross-border cooperation is institutionalized and agricultural systems are exposed to the same effects of climate change. This article therefore examines the existence of cross-border exchanges in the adaptation trajectories of farmers in the three countries. It is based on interviews with 35 farmers and 15 agricultural support professionals. The results reveal very few cross-border exchanges, and suggest several avenues to explain why thoughts on adaptation to climate change do not cross the borders more. Adapting to climate change could, however, be a common challenge that could form the basis of a cross-border region that would not only be institutional, but also functional, appropriated, and experienced.
publisher: Centre Interdisciplinaire d'Etudes et de Recherches sur l'Allemagne (CIERA)

title: Les voix de Marianne et Corinne traduites en allemand autour de 1800
abstract: This study reconsiders the context of production of two French novels translations into German around 1800, Marianen’s Begebenheiten by Friederike Helene Unger, and Corinna oder Italien by Dorothea Schlegel. Both translations were published by the same editor Unger. Enlightening the motivations of the editor implies to re-trace the reception’s history of the original versions and of their authors (Marivaux, De Staël), in France and Germany. The comparative analysis makes intellectual and supranational communities visible, in direct link with French-German transfers. The questioning of women condition that colors both originals, must be replaced in the context of emergence of women’s voices. These “original” women voices are here relayed by women translators beyond the original text.

title: Remapping the Senegambian megaliths: Beyond the culture area paradigm
abstract: Between 1969 and 1982, Victor Martin and Charles Becker led a series of reconnaissance missions to document thousands of sites for their Inventaire des Sites Protohistoriques de la Sénégambie. This dataset has since become a cornerstone in the archaeology of central Senegambia, where site distribution maps continue to define a “Megalith Zone” and provide context for excavations at well-known type-sites. However, we argue that spatial and quantitative data from the Inventaire can do more to help us envision megalithic sites as places embedded in complex social landscapes. We begin by exploring how the Inventaire emerged from and now perpetuates a culture area paradigm through mapping strategies of selection and simplification. We then advocate for a more relational paradigm in Senegambian archaeology by developing a critical cartography of megalithic sites recently digitized for MAEASaM (Mapping Africa’s Endangered Archaeological Sites and Monuments). Here we use recent survey results and geostatistical tools to assess and visualize uncertainties in the Inventaire, while also working to better illustrate megalithic monuments as material expressions of social interaction at multiple scales. In so doing, we emphasize how fresh approaches to “legacy” data from the Inventaire and similar spatial archives could aid with efforts to decolonize African archaeology.

title: The Mehlman archives and the archaeology of Nasera rockshelter, Tanzania
abstract: Archives are increasingly recognized as a critical element in archaeological research in eastern Africa and elsewhere that, unlike excavation, are a non-destructive source of information. However, the utility of any archive is dependent in part on its availability. We report here on the recent recovery of the archives of Michael J. Mehlman, who excavated at multiple important archaeological sites in northern Tanzania. Establishing clear plans for preservation, documentation, and data sharing are underway. In this article, archive materials from Mehlman’s work at the Middle and Later Stone Age site of Nasera rockshelter provide a starting point to assess the collection and its research potential and to gain a better understanding of the 1975–1976 excavations. Like other sites in eastern Africa, archaeological investigations at Nasera follow an approximate 42-year research cycle, emphasizing the need to preserve this collection and those that follow from it for future scholarly generations.

title: Reopening the archives of archaeology at Ile-Ife, Nigeria: Towards a history of the Osangangan Obamakin sacred grove
abstract: In 1953, the archaeologists Bernard Fagg and A.J.H. Goodwin excavated sacred grove sites in Ile-Ife, south-western Nigeria, where they hoped to uncover artefactual and stratigraphic evidence of the town’s early history. They were especially interested in developing artefact typologies and chronologies, as part of the systematisation of archaeology in Africa during this period. But far from primordial places conserving undisturbed records of past human practices, such sacred groves were dynamic spaces with complex histories where successive communities repeatedly remodified and reinterpreted earlier cultural features and their larger landscape. This article revisits the excavations of the grove of Osangangan Obamakin, drawing upon the largely unpublished records to address new questions about the grove’s early and recent past, and the significance of its archaeology to understanding the wider history of Ife’s cultural landscapes.

title: Les fouilles suisses à Tabo (1965-1974). Plongée dans la mémoire archivistique d’une mission archéologique au Soudan
abstract: The site of Tabo, the occupation of which spans from the 2nd millennium BCE to the Medieval (Christian) period, is in northern Sudan. It was excavated between 1965 and 1974 by a mission from the University of Geneva. The results of these archaeological investigations remain largely unpublished. This article provides an overview of the ongoing study of the archives and materials from these excavations. This project is the result of collaboration between the following institutions:- the Swiss-French-Sudanese Archaeological Mission of Kerma-Doukki Gel, which inherited the scientific intellectual property of Charles Bonnet’s works;- the Museum of Art and History in Geneva, where the artefacts from Tabo are housed; - the Natural History Museum of Geneva, which preserves the archaeozoological material; the University of Geneva, with the ARCAN laboratory (Faculty of Sciences), where the anthropological remains and documentary archives are stored; the Egyptology Unit (Faculty of Arts), which holds documents from the archives of Helen Jacquet-Gordon and Jean Jacquet.

title: The Archives of the Archaeological Survey of Sudanese Nubia (1963-1969): An overview
abstract: This article offers an overview of the archives of the Archaeological Survey of Sudanese Nubia, a large-scale survey and excavation mission carried out in northern Sudan from 1963 to 1969 in the context of the construction of the Aswan High Dam. It provides a brief presentation of the background to this fieldwork, describes the content of the archives produced during the campaign, and highlights the scientific and heritage value of their study and publication.

title: Writing Against History/Memory
abstract: This article links linguistic nationalism and print media by inspecting narratives from four newspapers popular in Assam, a northeast Indian state, at the time when spontaneous mobilizations against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019 peaked. Drawing from the vernacular and regional press, the article departs from the extant literature on the CAA, that mostly dwells on its constitutionality and legality. The present argument explores the scant studies on vernacular print media in Assam, the interplay between this media and collective memory, and the history of Assamese linguistic nationalism vis-à-vis Bengali. With the political crisis activating “memory frames” that viewed the CAA as an “event,” these narratives went far beyond just demands for repealing the law. The article argues that it rekindled colonial-era narratives of “linguistic domination” by Bengali in Assam and aroused fears, real or exaggerated, of the Assamese language and identity becoming extinct. The print media also reflected historical grievances according to which Assam is a neglected and oppressed state. The article paints a complex picture of the anti-CAA stir in Assam with language at its center harboring deep historical concerns that go beyond the recent political shifts and Hindu/Muslim or citizen/foreigner binaries.

title: Argument marking strategies in tropative constructions
abstract: This article examines the results of a study on strategies for marking arguments in tropative constructions (i.e., expressing meanings such as “X considers Y to be Z” (direct) or “Y is considered to be Z” (reverse), where X is the subject, Y is the object, and Z is a characteristic) of 215 languages, including natural languages, constructed languages, and languages occupying an intermediate position between the two. The study used online elicitation method to collect translations from native speakers and language users. For 27 % of the languages, it was found that at least two of the three arguments (or, more rarely, all the arguments) are encoded in the same way. A number of languages (like Latin, Karaim, and Aymara) displayed different marking of the characteristic depending on the construction type. Typical tropative models were overviewed, with a focus on the argument marking strategies in direct vs. reverse and positive vs. negative (“X does not consider Y to be Z” or “Y is not considered to be Z”) constructions.

title: Control measures regarding the audit of supervised entities complying with legislative statutes and legal acts of the Russian Federation in the field of state defense order
abstract: Since military spending has become increasingly integral to Russia’s economy, the expenditures on goods produced under the state defense order have escalated sharply. As a consequence, the risks of errors or economic crimes in the military sphere have also increased, making it necessary to develop a clear methodology for control measures that could minimize them. This article is motivated by the absence of a consistent methodology in Russian legal acts and the existence of a large but fragmented body of laws, regulatory acts, and recommendations defining the standards for control measures to be taken in connection with the state defense order. The analysis is based on a collection of relevant documents providing guidance on the conduct of such measures (financial control), particularly with respect to the expenditures on raw inputs, materials, auxiliary inputs, semi-finished products, and purchased components included by the supervised entity in a price proposal for fulfilling the state defense order. The main problems and violations encountered in price formation are identified, and a set of audit activities for controlling and verifying these expenditures is proposed.

title: Personified images of the supreme power in late imperial Russia as reflected in Soviet memoirs between the 1950s and 1960s (Alexander II, Alexander III, and Nicholas II)
abstract: This article examines the personified representations of Alexander II, Alexander III, and Nicholas II in Soviet memoirs between the 1950s and 1960s by focusing on how the recollections of those who witnessed the Russian Empire through its final upheavals shaped the perceptions of the last Russian emperors through the lens of Soviet ideology and personal experience. The mechanisms underlying both positive and negative portrayals of the monarchs and reflecting the interplay between the political landscape of the time and the personal experiences of the memoirists are outlined. The formation of the Soviet historical consciousness under the conditions of a shift in the historical memory paradigm during the Khrushchev Thaw is traced. It is concluded that Soviet memoir literature of the studied period departed from the earlier established confrontational narrative on key figures of the Russian autocracy of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

title: Linguocultural parameters of the influence exercised by St. Petersburg’s image in online restaurant advertising on the Chinese linguistic identity
abstract: This article presents the results of a study on the linguistic means used to shape St. Petersburg’s image in online restaurant advertising aimed at the Chinese audience. The advertising texts were collected from the official websites of ten Chinese restaurants in St. Petersburg and analyzed by the discursive, linguocultural, and linguopragmatic methods. The analysis revealed the main linguistic strategies and tactics of shaping St. Petersburg’s image, among which the central ones are the appeal to Chinese cultural heritage and the promotion of cultural synthesis, authenticity, and exclusive gastronomic experience. All these strategies were found to be implemented through a wide range of linguistic means, including lexical units with spatial semantics, markers of the city’s settings and characteristics, and tropes. The findings suggest that the multiculturalism of St. Petersburg is reflected not only in its physical urban space but also in the virtual environment constructed through specific linguistic means, thus contributing to the development of intercultural communication theory, linguoculturology, marketing linguistics, and place branding.

title: Semantic changes in person-denoting nouns within denotative and ideographic groups of words in the field of medicine
abstract: Semantic word production is one of the main ways of coining new words in the Russian language. Using the data from Russian dictionaries compiled at different times, this article explores the semantic potential of the denotative category of nouns that refer to specific aspects in the field of medicine. The results obtained suggest that person-denoting nouns can integrate into multiple derivational models simultaneously, thus demonstrating that any language is a structured system in which all components are interconnected and influence each other. Several productive derivational semantic models for creating new meanings of contemporary Russian words are identified. These models are based on various semantic processes, such as modification of existing meanings and metaphorical and metonymic transfer, with metaphorical reinterpretation emerging as the most productive mechanism of semantic derivation within the studied group of words.

title: “Invisible” or “inaccessible”: The problem of contacting the king in the Achaemenid Empire
abstract: In this article, the phenomenon of “invisibility” / “inaccessibility” of the Persian kings in the Achaemenid Empire and its coverage in ancient historiography are examined. Particular attention is paid to the works of Herodotus, Ctesias of Cnidus, Xenophon, and other classical authors who explored the social, political, and cultural aspects of royal isolation. The origins and evolution of this tradition are traced. Its connections with the ideologies of the Median and Assyrian monarchies are analyzed. The pragmatic reasons for restricting access to the king, such as security measures, court etiquette, and social hierarchy within the royal court, are identified. The findings suggest that the “invisibility” of the Persian kings was more a result of ancient stereotypes and pragmatic concerns than a deliberate policy of placing monarchs in complete isolation.

title: An integrative model for the analysis of taxis in German prepositional-deverbative constructions
abstract: An integrative model, combining existing fragmented linguistic descriptions, was developed for analyzing prepositional-deverbative constructions (PDC) in modern German as a core means of expressing taxis relations. The four-level analytical framework was consistently implemented using a corpus of selected linguistic data. Its explanatory value was demonstrated based on a representative sample of utterances containing prepositional deverbatives collected from the Leipzig National Corpus of modern German. This representative sample was analyzed to show how an interaction between the studied levels determines the expression of the taxis relations of simultaneity and non-simultaneity (i.e., to indicate whether actions happen at the same time or at different times). According to the proposed approach, the PDC emerges as a dynamic semantic-syntactic system, the integral meaning of which is formed through a non-linear integration of the following interconnected components: 1) the word-formation level: the degree of verbogenicity of the deverbative; 2) the lexical-aspectual level: the aspectual-actional class semantics of the deverbative; 3) the relational level: the categorical semantics of the prepositional classifier; 4) the contextual-modulation level: the influence of the semantics of the main predicate, determinants, and pragmatic conditions of the discourse.

title: Defining cross-sectoral criteria to classify compensation obligations
abstract: This article examines the criteria used in Russian civil jurisprudence to classify relations related to making up for the distress and inconvenience due to the troubles caused (compensation obligations). Specifically, such criteria that take into account the cross-sectoral nature of compensation obligations are outlined. The results obtained suggest that compensation obligations can be categorized based on both their structural elements, as is normally done for tort obligations, and some other important criteria. Furthermore, our overview of common classification approaches reveals the cross-sectoral nature of compensation obligations and demonstrates that they can take the forms of either monetary awards or requirements for certain legal actions.

title: General theoretical problems of constitutional legal relations
abstract: The enduring problems of a correlation between the general theory of law and various specific branches of legal science have recently received much attention. Reconsidering this correlation from the perspective of modern political and legal paradigms would bring about more effective systemic connections between different legal disciplines. In this context, of particular importance is the connection between the general theory of state and law and constitutional law, which is most clearly manifested at the level of legal relations. The results of a general theoretical analysis carried out at three levels of constitutional legal relations (general, specific, and actual) make it possible to revise the “human–state–business” relation using the basic provision of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, which recognizes the human being as the highest value.

title: Differentiation of criminal liability for environmental crimes
abstract: This article analyzes the constituent elements of environmental offenses. It argues that the terms “crimes against the environment” and “environmental crimes” can be treated as synonyms, considering that the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation recognizes the natural environment as a legitimate object of protection when defining the tasks of criminal law (see Part 1 of Article 2) and regulates environmental issues in Chapter 26 of its Special Part, entitled “Environmental Crimes.” The differentiation of criminal liability is also governed primarily by the provisions of the Special Part of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, which distinguish among its grounds, limits, and forms based on the nature, typical degree of public danger of the offense, and typical personality traits of the offender. The Special Part of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation generally relies on qualifying circumstances when applying liability rules. However, these factors cannot be the only criteria in making decisions about liability. Given the intrinsic worth and benefits of environmental protection for both individuals and society as a whole, the elements of environmental crimes should be set out in a separate section, following Section VIII “Crimes Against the Economy” of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation. The analysis shows that recent legislative developments have expanded the number of qualifying elements of environmental crimes, which are commonly used to differentiate the liability for environmental wrongdoing.

title: Development of the state administration bodies providing healthcare in Russian Turkestan (1867–1917)
abstract: By the 19th century, Russia had clinical medicine and provided essential healthcare services to its population. In newly acquired regions, the imperial government acted as an active transmitter of medical knowledge and billed it as beneficial for everyone. Since Russian Turkestan (Turkestan Governorate-General) was remote and lacked local pharmacies or medical facilities at that time, a unique healthcare management system was developed there. Using the materials of the Russian State Military Historical Archive and the Complete Collection of the Laws of the Russian Empire, this article examines the main differences in the delivery of healthcare services between Russian Turkestan and other parts of the Russian Empire during the period between 1867 and 1917. The results show that the region’s healthcare was managed by the military-controlled public authorities (i.e., the military department controlled all civil affairs, including medical administration). The key managing body was the District Military Medical Directorate headed by the local chief medical officer.

title: Herodotus’ Tyrsenian Logos as a source of Classical Greek views on the Pelasgians
abstract: The perception of the Pelasgians and Tyrsenians by the ancient Greeks is analyzed based on the Tyrsenian Logos, a part of Herodotus’ Histories that claims the Lydian origin of the Tyrsenians. The existing scholarly interpretations of the Tyrsenian Logos are critically evaluated. Particular attention is paid to R. Drews’ theory of the Etruscan migration to the Aegean, which is engraved in the memory of the Hellenes and recorded by Herodotus. The study reveals that Herodotus’ version was not supported by other Classical authors. Therefore, these ideas about the link between the Lydians and the Tyrsenians had no influence on Greek thought before the Hellenistic period. A careful analysis of other parts of the text indicates inconsistencies in Herodotus’ views on the genesis of the Tyrsenians, as well as no concrete proof for the link between the Lydian origin of the Tyrsenians and the Pelasgians of the presumably Tyrsenian Lemnos.

title: The New York Times newspaper in the political space of the United States between the 1850s and 1860s
abstract: In this article, the historical path of The New York Times, a prominent US newspaper, on the eve of the American Civil War is traced. Its establishment, development, and rise to become a major force in US politics are examined against the US political landscape before the Civil War, including the US presidential election of 1860 and the growing conflict between the North and the South. Particular attention is paid to the role of H.J. Raymond, who founded the newspaper, in boosting its popularity throughout his journalistic and political career. The following distinguishing characteristics of the newspaper were identified: striving for the highest level of objectivity possible, ensuring that its reporting is accurate, and providing a platform for different interpretations and diverse voices. All these features enabled the newspaper to strengthen and solidify its voice on the national scene by the late 1850s and early 1860s.

title: Dynamics of meaning generation in the textual space of literary discourse: Cognitive semantic potential of metaphorization
abstract: This article examines the process of metaphorization and its cognitive semantic potential within the textual space of literary discourse. The text analyzed is A. Christie’s novel “The Mirror Crack’d from Side to Side.” The results show that the metaphors used by the author generate new meanings based on the non-referential nature of the compared objects, and it significantly broadens the range of contexts in which they are used in the novel: rather than serving only as markers of the author’s individual style or as expressive means, which can, to a certain extent, transform the semantics of textual units of various sizes, they function as cognitive semantic mechanisms that structure the fictional reality. Based on the obtained results, it is concluded that metaphorization reflects the author’s individual worldview shaped by ethnoand linguacultural factors, whereas the background knowledge of the reader, interacting with the author, enables the decoding of the complexes of meanings and expands the cognitive semantic potential of the components of the textual space of literary discourse.

title: Japan–Philippines maritime security cooperation (2011–2024): shaping an emerging military alliance in the Asia-Pacific
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific and the growing limitations of regional security mechanisms, maritime security cooperation between Japan and the Philippines from 2011 to 2024 has emerged as a strategic alignment that has attracted considerable attention across the region. Drawing on historical analysis, synthesis, and a review of relevant academic literature, this article elucidates the evolution, substantive dimensions, and strategic significance of Japan–Philippines relations. It argues that this relationship has increasingly approximated a quasi-alliance model, contributing to stronger deterrence and the consolidation of a rules-based maritime order, although it has not yet reached the level of a formal military alliance.

title: From global vision to the construction of national identity: conceptual metaphors in Vietnam’s policy discourse at University of Oxford
abstract: This research examines how conceptual metaphors in the official English translation of General Secretary Tô Lâm’s policy address at Oxford University construct a modern sense of nationhood within world affairs. Rather than using traditional description alone, it integrates Conceptual Metaphor Theory with Critical Discourse Analysis to examine the full English-language transcript of the speech. The MIP identification procedure helped detect figurative expressions, revealing 112 instances categorized into different dominant conceptual frames. These metaphorical mappings appear most frequently when articulating national strategy and the Vietnam-UK partnership, indicating they function as cognitive and persuasive mechanisms rather than stylistic decoration. The findings demonstrate a discursive shift from war-memory identity toward a future-oriented, innovation-driven, and co-creative international persona, showing metaphor to be central in shaping Vietnam’s global diplomatic visibility and agency.
