title: AI-Driven Translation Education: Opportunities and Challenges for Personalized Learning
abstract: In recent years, the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in language education and translation practice has aroused wide concern. However, the gap between the research and practice on its role in driving personalized translation learning still exists. This paper takes the impact of AI on personalized translation learning as the theme, systematically analyzing the AI's value in translation education, the current limitations, and future improvement directions. The main finding of this paper is that AI technology can support translation learning by providing instant feedback and data analysis, while it still faces challenges in unstable technology, the marginalization of teachers and ethical risks. Based on this, this paper suggests optimizing the accuracy and data security of the AI model at the technical level, promoting the collaboration system between teachers and AI from an educational perspective, and cultivating the ability of learners to balance dependence and autonomy to achieve the sustainable development of personalized translation learning.

title: Voynich Script as Medieval Pharmaceutical Notation: Latin Case Morphology and Recipe Structure in an Encrypted 15th-Century Antidotarium
abstract: Building on botanical identifications of 34 plants in the Voynich Manuscript's herbal section (Paper 1), we present evidence that the accompanying Voynichese text encodes pharmaceutical recipes using an abbreviated Latin grammatical system. Analysis of 864 case-marked words reveals a five-case morphological system (-oy nominative, -am accusative, -an genitive, -ay dative, -ae ablative) consistent with medieval Latin. Statistical comparison shows the case distribution matches Latin pharmaceutical texts with high significance (χ² = 41.56, p < 0.003; Monte Carlo probability of chance occurrence: 0.26%). Application route markers (9h = external use, 9k = internal use) predict the expected medical application of identified plants with 94.1% accuracy. Recipe structure analysis confirms verb-initial patterns matching the Antidotarium Nicolai "Recipe" (Rx) convention. Cross-reference with Circa Instans plant nomenclature identifies 12 vocabulary correspondences. Cross-validation with the manuscript's pharmaceutical section (2,389 words) confirms identical patterns, supporting a unified notation system. We propose that Voynichese functions as a specialized pharmaceutical shorthand, combining Latin grammatical inflection with logograms and semantic markers—not a natural language cipher but a notation system analogous to modern pharmaceutical abbreviations.

title: A Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript's Botanical and Illustrated Sections: Evidence for Northern Italian Origin
abstract: The Voynich Manuscript (Yale Beinecke MS 408) has resisted decipherment since its rediscovery in 1912. This study presents a comprehensive morphological analysis of the manuscript's illustrated sections, examining 79 folios containing botanical, pharmaceutical, balneological, zodiacal, and cosmological content. Using diagnostic feature analysis and comparison with securely dated medieval herbals, we identify 34 plant species with 23 achieving HIGH confidence. Critically, we find zero anachronistic (New World) plants among the identifications, with all claimed New World species having morphologically superior Old World alternatives. Geographic distribution analysis reveals a distinctive Alpine-Mediterranean species overlap pattern that uniquely indicates Northern Italian (Veneto) origin. Cross-referencing with the Codex Bellunensis and other 15th-century Italian herbals confirms consistency with regional manuscript traditions. Our findings support the radiocarbon date range (1404-1438 CE) and establish the manuscript as a genuine medieval European medical compendium rather than a modern forgery or post-Columbian work.

title: MORPHSS WP 1 Literature review protocol
abstract: Literature review protocol for MORPHSS Work Package 1: Cataloguing open research practices in the humanities and social sciences. This document details the approach taken to conducting a literature review to inform initial work on the MORPHSS (Materialising Open Research Practices in the Humanities and Social Sciences) project; in particular, Work Package 1 (Cataloguing open research practices in the humanities and social sciences).

title: Proprietà di Radon-Nikodym e Derivazione di Misure: Teorema di Decomposizione di Lebesgue e Misure Mutuamente Singolari
abstract: La teoria della misura astratta, sviluppatasi nel corso del ventesimo secolo principalmente grazie ai contributi fondamentali di Henri Lebesgue, Johann Radon, Otton Nikodym e altri matematici di straordinaria levatura, rappresenta uno dei pilastri più solidi e raffinati dell'analisi matematica moderna...

title: “A fin de que se eduquen y no padezcan necesidad”. Infancia en la Casa de la Doctrina de Pamplona (1792-1798)
abstract: El presente artículo analiza un conjunto de 120 memoriales relativos a la Casa de la Doctrina de Pamplona, en los que se solicita acceso para niños y niñas de entre 7 y 12 años durante la última década del siglo XVIII. Los datos recopilados en ellos, junto con las informaciones identificadas en los libros de registro, ofrecen una panorámica amplia sobre los perfiles de los usuarios y su entorno. A través del análisis documental, se explorará el papel desempeñado por la Casa de la Doctrina a la hora de aliviar las situaciones de necesidad y las repercusiones que el paso por el establecimiento tenía para sus jóvenes usuarios. Asimismo, una de las virtudes de los memoriales es que permite analizar las vulnerabilidades esgrimidas por los solicitantes, aquellas con las que justificaban el ingreso de los pequeños en el establecimiento. Ello ofrece una perspectiva muy elocuente sobre las dificultades a las que se enfrentan los sectores sociales más desfavorecidos para mantener y educar a sus hijos, así como sobre las estrategias desplegadas para hacer frente a dichas circunstancias.

title: Tripulaciones de la Real Armada española en el siglo XVIII. Pobreza e incertidumbre salarial
abstract: En esta investigación se propone como objetivo el comprobar la situación de pobreza en la que se encuentra un colectivo socio-profesional peculiar como es el de las tripulaciones de los barcos de la Real Armada española en la segunda mitad del siglo XVIII. Acreditar hasta qué punto el tópico de la pobreza se verifica y, en especial, analizar la incertidumbre económica de unos hombres que padecen de un retraso significativo para el cobro de sus salarios. Para el estudio se analizarán los testamentos de esta marinería que se conservan en el Archivo Histórico Provincial de Cádiz (España), en concreto los recogidos por el escribano mayor de marina de la localidad de San Fernando, donde se ubicaba uno de los tres arsenales de la Armada y localización de la jefatura del Departamento Marítimo de Cádiz.

title: Redes de confianza del artesanado platero en el sureste español, siglos XVIII y XIX: padrinos y albaceas
abstract: Este artículo analiza las redes de confianza del artesanado platero en el sureste español durante los siglos XVIII y XIX. A partir del estudio de documentación parroquial y notarial, se examinan las figuras del padrino y del albacea como nodos clave en los vínculos sociales más estrechos de estos trabajadores. El objetivo principal es explorar las relaciones entre el grupo profesional y su red social, así como proponer el concepto de confianza como mecanismo de articulación social frente a riesgos e incertidumbres. ¿Quiénes ocuparon estas posiciones centrales, cuál fue su procedencia y qué funciones desempeñaron? Estas son las preguntas fundamentales que guían la investigación.

title: The Invisibility of the Black Working Class in Early Films (1890s-1930s): The Case of Pennsylvania
abstract: This article explores the historical invisibility of the Black working class in early American cinema, focusing on Pennsylvania between the 1890s and 1930s. Drawing on African American studies, film studies and labor studies, it examines how films from this period reinforced racialized conceptions of the working class by excluding or distorting the image of Black laborers. From Siegmund Lubin’s racially coded comedies to the race film The Scar of Shame (1929) and the pre-Code classic Baby Face (1933), the study traces how cinema shaped public perceptions of race and class. It highlights the persistent absence of Black working-class protagonists, especially in narratives rooted in Northern industrial regions, and argues for a regional approach to film history that re-centers marginalized voices. Ultimately, the article reveals how early film culture contributed to a dominant vision of the working class as white—an exclusion still echoed in contemporary representations.

title: La présence des mouches : surgissements d’animaux dans les Pensées
abstract: La présence des mouches: animals appearing in Pascal’s Pensées. Animals, in Pascal’s Pensées, are both mechanized (even reified) and presentified, particularly through their sensory impact (visual, auditory). But their modes of presence sometimes go beyond what could be constituted as a “Pascalian conception of the animal” and reveal, in flashes of insight that transcend theoretical thought, the outlines of an experiential conception of the animal. In other words, the animals in the Pensées are both elements of theoretical thought and forces of emergence born of direct or bookish experience. In this respect, they function as major crystallization points for the complex and ambiguous relationships that Pascal establishes with Jesuit discourses, as well as Descartes and Montaigne.

title: Le théâtre des livres : bibliomanie et citations dans Les Provinciales de Pascal
abstract: The theatre of books: bibliomania and quotations in Pascal’s Les Provinciales. The quotation is neither ornamental nor merely entertaining in Les Provinciales: above all, it is at the core of a new poetics of quotation, of formidable ingenuity, repurposing the ironic procedures of the burlesque novel for the technical terrain of grace and morality. The article focuses primarily on the first ten letters (before the modes of condemnation become more explicit), examining the ostensive rhetoric of the good Jesuit Father, the argumentative manipulations, and the significance of repetition at the heart of the quotation, in order to reveal the spiritual dimension underlying the ways in which quotations are used.

title: Indigenous Participation: Canada’s Trade for Reconciliation
abstract: The constitutional recognition of reconciliation has paved the way for the integration of the Crown’s domestic obligations toward Indigenous peoples into Canada’s international commitments. In this context, trade policy has emerged as an additional avenue through which the national objective of reconciliation may be advanced. This paper examines the incorporation of Indigenous peoples’ rights and interests in six Canadian trade agreements concluded following the launch of Canada’s Progressive Trade Agenda. It analyzes the normative innovations introduced and evaluates the extent to which these agreements move beyond symbolic recognition toward meaningful participation. While the degree of integration varies across agreements, the findings suggest that Canadian trade policy increasingly reflects an effort to align international economic governance with the domestic imperative of reconciliation.

title: Linking employee motivation and engagement: A bibliometric review
abstract: Employee motivation and engagement are interrelated constructs that are critical to productivity, job satisfaction, and employee retention. Although both topics have been thoroughly studied, their theoretical and thematic intersections have not yet been systematically defined. This study uses 2,169 peer-reviewed journal articles to provide a bibliometric analysis of research on employee motivation and engagement from 1972 to 2025. Using the R Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and Biblioshiny packages, we examine publication trends, important authors and journals, thematic structures, and collaboration networks. The findings indicate significant growth in output and a transition from initial research on organizational commitment and work attitudes to engagement-focused frameworks based on job demands-resources theory and associated organizational and social exchange theories. Keyword and co-citation networks indicate that motivation, employee engagement, work engagement, organizational commitment, and job satisfaction form the conceptual core of the field and are closely related to performance, well-being, and burnout. Future paths that connect engagement and motivation to broader organizational and societal issues include gamification, digital and hybrid work, corporate social responsibility, green HRM, and employee well-being. This review raises issues that require further research and provides insightful material for framing both academic research and evidence-based work practices.

title: LE MARKETING DES SERVICES SPECIFIQUE AUX COMPAGNIES D’ASSURANCE : CAS (SAA, CASH, CIAR, ET TRUST)
abstract: Dans le présent article, nous analysons les pratiques marketing des compagnies d’assurance   suivantes : la saa, la cash, la ciar et la trust. surtout dans notre pays qui se caractérise par l’absence d’une culture d’assurance. L’information est obtenue par le biais d’entretien semi-directif. Les données ont fait l’objet d’une analyse de contenu thématique. Car nous souhaiterions essentiellement découvrir la véritable nature des comportements marketing des compagnies d’assurance. Nous avons conclus que le marketing constitue la meilleure solution pour développer le marché algérien des assurances.

title: DES DISPARITÉS DE GENRE DANS L’ACTIVITÉ ÉCONOMIQUE REMUNÉRÉE DANS LES PAYS DE LA CEMAC : ANALYSE COMPARÉE DES CAS DU CAMEROUN, DU CONGO ET DU GABON
abstract: Cet article vise à estimer et à expliquer la différence de probabilité d’accès à une activité économique rémunérée entre hommes et femmes au Cameroun, au Congo et au Gabon. Sur les bases de données de l’EESI_2010 au Cameroun, de l’EDS_2012 au Congo et de l’EDS_2012 au Gabon., nous utilisons la décomposition globale et détaillée de Blinder - Oaxaca (1973). Nous trouvons que cette différence de probabilité est de 20 points en faveur des hommes au Cameroun, expliquée à 56,15% par la discrimination ; de 16 points au Gabon due à 83,73% à la discrimination ; et de 5 points au Congo due à 72,40% à la discrimination. Nous trouvons que dans ces pays cette discrimination des femmes s’explique par des variables telles : l’âge, le niveau d’instruction, la religion, le statut matrimonial et le nombre d’enfants de 5 à 14 ans vivant dans le ménage

title: IMPACT DU TOURISME CULTUREL SUR LE DÉVELOPPEMENT DURABLE EN TUNISIE
abstract: In a gloomy context dominated by economic, political and social crises, tourism in Tunisia badly requires restructuring or even reform. Given the precariousness of seaside tourism, this sector has to draw its resources from other more attractive and diversified factors. This problematic context urged our attempts to apprehend cultural tourism from a Probit model that implements a few variables in direct and indirect relation with an alternative tourism based on heritage, cultural experience, nationality and number of overnight stays.   Using individual data from a sample of 1500 customers who visited Tunisia during the summer holidays of 2015, we tried to interpret the seemingly very suggestive results. These findings show that culture, heritage, cultural experience, nationality and number of overnight stays during a previous experience may form a full system that could promote cultural tourism as well as support sustainable development in Tunisia

title: Cultural Intelligence and the theory of planned behavior in predicting work-abroad intentions: evidence from Vietnamese students in Australia
abstract: This study integrates Cultural Intelligence (CQ) - specifically motivational and behavioral dimensions - with the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to examine the intention to work abroad among Vietnamese students in Australia. Using data from 361 participants, analysis was conducted through SPSS 26 and SmartPLS 4.0 under a PLS-SEM framework. Results show that both TPB constructs and CQ components significantly influence work-abroad intention. Multicultural experience (MCE) significantly moderates the relationship between CQ and intention. Additionally, CQ moderates the effects of attitude and perceived behavioral control but not subjective norm. The study contributes theoretically by combining TPB and CQ into a unified model. Practical implications are proposed to support educational institutions and workforce development programs in preparing young talent for global employment.

title: The impact of religiosity on corporate debt structure
abstract: This study examines the impact of religious beliefs on corporate debt structure using a regression model applied to a dataset comprising 485 firms across 10 countries over the period 2009–2022. The results indicate that, while firms operating in countries with higher levels of religiosity tend to rely more on long-term debt, religious beliefs do not have a significant effect on firms’ short-term debt decisions. In addition, we show that the positive effect of religiosity on long-term debt is less pronounced for firms with higher ratio of institutional ownership and more pronounced in countries with better control for the corruption. Our main findings remain robust when alternative measures of the dependent variable and alternative model specifications are employed. This study contributes to the literature on the relationship between religiosity and corporate debt structure, while also providing practical implications for other stakeholders.

title: Berättande och trauma i Christina Wahldéns Kort kjol
abstract: Mycket lite akademisk uppmärksamhet har riktats mot Christina Wahldéns ungdomsroman Kort kjol (1998), trots dess utbredda användning i svenska skolor. Romanen är hittills det enda svenska fall där en föräldradriven rörelse, på liknande sätt som i USA, lyckats få igenom ett skolförbud av en bok på grund av dess skildring av våldtäkt. Syftet med denna artikel är att utöka kunskapen om Wahldéns våldtäktsskildring genom en kontextualiserande, narratologisk analys som placerar våldtäktsscenen i relation till romanen som helhet. Artikeln argumenterar för att Kort kjol bör förstås inom den feministiska tradition som sedan 1970-talet framgångsrikt etablerat en typ av berättelse som fokaliserar sexuellt våld ur offrets perspektiv, vilket möjliggör berättelser där smärta, vrede och samhällskritik tar plats. Artikeln utforskar likheterna mellan Wahldéns berättelse och Judith Hermans feministiskt informerade, psykologiska, konceptualisering av trauma och argumenterar för att Kort kjol bedriver en metakritik av vanligt förekommande scenarier, där kontrollen över berättelsen tas ifrån offret. Medan huvudpersonens berättande framställs som hjälpsamt i trygga relationer där lyssnaren reagerar utan att döma, antyder romanen att det upprepade berättandet om våldtäkten som förväntas av huvudpersonen under den utdragna rättsprocessen ytterligare traumatiserar offret. Analysen visar att Kort kjol framställer berättande och lyssnande som helt avgörande sociala aktiviteter som kan få både återtraumatiserande och stärkande effekter – beroende på kontext. I ljuset av ”banned books”-rörelsens tendens att felaktigt kategorisera alla typer av böcker som berör sexualitet eller sexuellt våld som pornografiska, påvisar artikeln vikten av att förvalta en narratologisk kompetens i läsningar av litteratur om våldtäkt, där fokaliseringens helt centrala roll tas i beaktande. Artikeln drar slutsatsen att Kort kjol, genom att skildra hur offer för sexuellt våld kan ta kontroll över sin egen berättelse, men också tystas genom andras motberättelser, belyser de kulturella och institutionella strukturer som möjliggör, och ibland försvårar, etisk kommunikation om sexuellt våld.

title: Ingen lämplig låt för barn
abstract: Artikeln undersöker varför Thomas Stenströms låt ”Slå mig hårt i ansiktet” (Larsson, Humlén & Stenström, 2014) trots sin popularitet väckte krav på stopp i radio och tv samt förbud i skolan. Syftet är att visa hur kritiken grundas på sångens retoriska och estetiska utformning samt formas av de situationer där den hörs. Materialet omfattar låttexten, anmälningar till Granskningsnämnden för radio och tv, mediedebatten samt reaktioner från föräldrar och från en rektor. Analysen utgår från teorier om den retoriska situationen samt från perspektivet på sånglyrik som muntligt och performativt uttryck. Resultaten visar att mottagandet är situerat. I familjeprofilerade medier uppfattas våldsmetaforerna som ett hot i en samhällskontext präglad av våld, medan de i skolan kopplas till föreställningar om barndomens oskuld, skolans värdegrundsuppdrag och vuxnas ansvar. Kritiken riktas främst mot titeln och mot återkommande hakar, där metaforer tolkas bokstavligt och antas kunna leda till handling. Den textnära analysen visar dock att sången rymmer en mer komplex retorik, där våldsmetaforer uttrycker intensitet och begär snarare än uppmaningar. Kritiken speglar därmed förr samtida normer och rädslor än textens faktiska innehåll. Artikeln framhåller också populärmusikens texter som en form av ungdomslitteratur och pekar på didaktiska strategier för att förstå textens retorik, genuskoder och tematik som mer konstruktiva svar än förbud.

title: HOW SUITABLE ARE NDO-LID AND PGL-I IN RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TESTS FOR SCREENING OF LEPROSY? A REVIEW OF DIAGNOSTIC STUDIES
abstract: Background: Indonesia has the third highest prevalence of leprosy, a neglected tropical disease caused by the “Mycobacterium leprae complex which causes neuropathy and hypopigmented skin lesions with hypoesthesia. The main problem in eradicating leprosy is due to its negative social stigma and prevalence in lower socioeconomic populations, as the gold standard for leprosy diagnosis is histopathology of skin smears. Hence, cost and time effective screening tools are needed. PGL-I and NDO-LID are antigens that have been developed as biomarkers used in serological assays, one of them being rapid lateral flow tests. Therefore, a rapid test utilizing a combination of PGL-I and NDO-LID as its marker is potentially a suitable tool for leprosy screening in areas with limited access to healthcare. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic potential of PGL-I and NDO-LID in rapid lateral flow tests for leprosy. Methods: This literature review was done by using the search engines PubMed, Science Direct, and SpringerLink. Results: Diagnostic potential studies for PGL-I rapid tests using UCP-LFA and Gold-LFA showed high overall sensitivity and specificity for leprosy patients, with more positive results in MB and PB patients. NDO-LID rapid test diagnostic studies which used the also showed similar results. However, these tests are not as accurate as ELISA and histopathology, but modifications such as additional biomarkers can be used to improve its utility. Conclusion: PGL-I and NDO-LID have good sensitivity and specificity from the results of various diagnostic studies, thus are potentially suitable for field screening of leprosy.

title: TRANSFORMING MDR-TB TREATMENT: EVIDENCE FOR SHORTER, SAFER, AND COST-SAVING REGIMENS WITH BPAL
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health challenge, with multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) contributing substantially to poor outcomes. Conventional regimens span 18–24 months, leading to limited adherence and treatment success. Shorter treatment regimens (STRs), such as the BPaL regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid), have emerged as promising alternatives. This systematic review assessed the efficacy, safety, and economic impact of 6-month STRs for drug-resistant TB. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched for studies published between 2021 and 2025. Eligible studies included clinical trials, cohort studies, and economic evaluations of regimens lasting ≤6 months. Study quality was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Tools. Results: Five studies met the inclusion criteria. BPaL regimens consistently achieved high treatment success rates (>80%), with faster sputum conversion and lower mortality compared with conventional injectable-based regimens. For example, one study in Thailand reported 82.1% favorable outcomes with BPaL versus 61–65% with standard long regimens. The all-oral BPaL regimen was generally well tolerated, with substantially fewer serious adverse events such as ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Economic evaluations demonstrated significant cost savings for both health systems and patients, alongside gains in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) averted. Conclusion: Six-month, all-oral BPaL regimens are effective, safer, and more cost-efficient than conventional MDR-TB therapies. Despite challenges related to drug availability and the infrastructure needed to monitor adverse events, the evidence strongly supports their accelerated global implementation to improve MDR-TB outcomes.

title: MAPPING THE GLOBAL SCIENTIFIC LANDSCAPE OF COLORECTAL CANCER AND VITAMIN D3 RESEARCH: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, with rising incidence in developing countries. Vitamin D3 has been implicated in colorectal cancer development, regulating cell proliferation, apoptosis, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Despite the growing body of literature, a comprehensive bibliometric analysis integrating colorectal cancer and vitamin D3 is still limited, highlighting a need to map research trends and collaboration patterns. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate global research trends, thematic structures, and collaboration networks in colorectal cancer and vitamin D3 research to identify hotspots and gaps. Methods: A quantitative bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database with the TITLE-ABS-KEY query: (“colorectal cancer” OR “colorectal carcinoma” OR “colorectal neoplasm” OR “colon cancer” OR “rectal cancer”) AND (“vitamin D3” OR cholecalciferol OR “25-hydroxyvitamin D3” OR calcitriol). Publications from 2015–2025 in English, including articles and reviews, were included. Data were analyzed using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny to assess publication trends, country- and author-level output, co-authorship networks, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. Results: Publication output peaked in 2020–2021, with the United States and China leading contributions. Munoz, A., Bostick, R.M., and Zhang, Y. were the most prolific authors. Keyword analysis revealed two main clusters: molecular mechanisms (VDR, calcitriol, Wnt/β-catenin) and clinical studies (vitamin D3 supplementation, serum concentration, trials). Thematic mapping indicated mature molecular research, active clinical translation, and emerging topics. Conclusion: Colorectal cancer research balances well-established molecular insights with evolving clinical applications. Concentrated output in high-capacity countries and underrepresentation in high-burden regions highlight opportunities for capacity building, international collaboration, and evidence-based prevention strategies.

title: AN ANALYTICAL STUDY OF EXCLUSIVE BREASTFEEDING IN RELATION TO INFANT GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT
abstract: Background: Breastfeeding plays a crucial role in fulfilling the nutritional needs of infants for optimal growth and development. WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding without adding other foods or drinks, for the first six months of a baby's life. Although the benefits of exclusive breastfeeding are widely known, exclusive breastfeeding is still not optimal. Objective: This purpose of this study to analyze the relationship between exclusive breastfeeding and the growth and development of infants aged 6-24 months at Puskesmas Palmerah. Methods: Using a cross-sectional design with a quantitative approach, this study involved 156 samples selected through consecutive non-probability sampling techniques and was conducted from January 2025 to February 2025. Data on the history of exclusive breastfeeding were collected through questionnaires, growth data were measured based on weight and height according to the WHO curve, and development was assessed using KPSP. Data analysis using the Chi-Square test. Conclusion: shows a significant relationship between exclusive breastfeeding and growth with p-value = 0.001 < 0.05 (based on weight-for-age), p-value = 0.006 < 0.05 (based on height-for-age), and p-value = 0.001 < 0.05 (based on weight-for-age). In addition, there's too a noteworthy relationship between elite breastfeeding and advancement with p-value = 0.000 (p<0.005). Thus, exclusive breastfeeding has a positive effect on infant growth and development. Efforts to increase the coverage of exclusive breastfeeding need to continue to be encouraged through education and support from health workers.

title: Translation Challenges of the Qur'an and Opportunities of integrating AI Automation
abstract: Despite the growing number of English translations of the Qur'an, persistent linguistic, semantic, rhetorical, and theological challenges continue to limit accurate comprehension for non-Arabic readers. Existing studies largely address these challenges descriptively or through comparative translation analysis, yet they seldom explore how recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly reasoning-based Large Language Models (LLMs), can systematically respond to the multidimensional complexity of Qur'anic language. This gap becomes critical in light of semantic shifts, polysemy, phonological symbolism, rhetorical devices, and doctrinal diversity that conventional translation methods struggle to accommodate. This study employs a qualitative-analytical approach grounded in Qur'anic linguistics, translation studies, and computational linguistics. It critically examines representative examples from English Qur'an translations to identify recurrent translation challenges, including lexical asymmetry, rhetorical loss, semantic ambiguity, and theological bias. Building on these findings, the paper proposes a conceptual AI framework that integrates multimodal embeddings, knowledge graphs, Qur'anic phonology, classical exegesis, theological schools, and historical context (Asbāb al-Nuzul), supported by explainable and anti-hallucination AI mechanisms. The results demonstrate that AI-assisted frameworks, when guided by authoritative Islamic knowledge sources and transparent reasoning models, have the potential to significantly enhance translation accuracy, semantic depth, and rhetorical sensitivity. Rather than replacing human scholarship, AI is positioned as an augmentative tool that bridges linguistic gaps while preserving interpretive plurality. The international impact of this research lies in its contribution to global Qur'anic studies, interfaith understanding, and ethical AI development. By proposing a multidisciplinary, culturally sensitive AI model, this study offers a scalable pathway for improving Qur'an translation, interpretation, and accessibility for diverse global audiences.

title: Generative AI in Corpus Linguistics: comparing ChatGPT-4 and manually developed NLP models for thematic concordance analysis
AI and Humanity: A Study of Ethical Concerns in Enthiran through the Perspective of AI Ethics Theory
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been an exploratory discipline and has begun to provoke ethical issues about humanity, which is why it is worth discussing AI Ethics Theory and Enthiran (2010). The paper is concerned with changing the lens through the perspective of AI Ethics Theory into the Indian Sci-fi Movie Enthiran. The film demonstrates the development and transformation of Chitti, a humanoid robot designed to assist human beings, who goes through a violent cycle of evolution after his ethical and moral limitations are lifted. This review of I discusses the ethical issues in the context of moral dilemmas, such as the duty of AI system designers, the serious threat of machines gaining autonomy, AI ethics, etc. When Chitti becomes a fully functional aide and a dysfunctional nightmare, one wonders whether AI systems are conscious and have free will and questions what the repercussions of the future development of technology in the absence of proper ethical control are. Therefore, the paper suggests a new legal ethic around AI, meaning this would help in establishing guidelines and preparing the legal system to ensure that AI systems advance. Taking the film Enthiran as a case study, this paper seeks to study the ethical dilemmas that AI poses in our lives and suggests how AI can be developed and carried out with responsibility and consideration for the safety and well-being of humans.

title: AI-Empowered Reconstruction of Higher Education Ecosystems Teaching Innovation, Management Transformation, and Implementation Pathways
abstract: With the rapid advancement of technologies such as generative AI and large language models (LLMs), artificial intelligence has evolved from an auxiliary tool to a core element within the higher education ecosystem. By systematically reviewing AI applications across higher education teaching domains (mathematics, foreign languages, physical education, etc.) and educational management domains (one-stop communities, student education, etc.), this study analyzes the underlying technical frameworks and value logic supporting AI. It reveals current shortcomings in humanities, technological limitations, application disparities, and other practical challenges. Concurrently, it emphasizes the construction of collaborative mechanisms, refinement of regulatory systems, and enhancement of competency cultivation across three dimensions, while optimizing and improving standardized frameworks.

title: Health Coaching for Chronic Disease Patients: A Thematic Literature Review
abstract: Health coaching has emerged as a promising intervention for managing chronic diseases, offering personalised support to improve health outcomes and quality of life. This thematic literature review synthesises findings from multiple sources to explore the effectiveness, implementation, and future directions of health coaching in chronic disease management. The review highlights the psychological and emotional benefits of health coaching, its effectiveness in managing specific chronic diseases such as cancer, motor neuron disease (MND), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and diabetes/obesity, and the evolving role of digitalisation and artificial intelligence (AI) in modern healthcare. Additionally, it offers insights into the coaching relationship, cultural competence, and the future of AI in coaching, providing a holistic perspective on the potential of health coaching in contemporary healthcare settings. Keywords: Health coaching, psychological well-being, behavioural change, patient-centred care, digitalisation, AI, emotional engagement

title: AI for the Humanities, Winter 2026
abstract: This syllabus is for a course taught during the Winter 2026 semester at Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah. The course was cross-listed across English, Editing and Publishing, Interdisciplinary Humanities, and Digital Humanities. The course was aimed at juniors and seniors studying in the Humanities. This was the first time the course was taught, and while the bones are good, I believe there are a number of ways to improve it in the future.

title: Spectres of medical AI: uncertainty, trust and the posthuman condition
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming clinical practice while simultaneously raising concerns about trust. Drawing on complexity theory, this paper argues that the crisis of trust in medical AI is rooted in multiple forms of uncertainty, including non-causal statistical relations, system-level complexity and the irreducibility of clinical judgement. It introduces a ‘U-map’ (Uncertainty Map), a conceptual tool that links specific forms of uncertainty to role-appropriate clinical uses such as screening, triage or deliberation aid. Using this map, the paper calibrates model claims against distinct clinical epistemic roles and develops a multidimensional account of trust that spans technological reliability, institutional governance and cultural–emotional orientations. On this basis, the paper sketches a posthuman model of care in which human–machine collaboration and distributed accountability offer a more adequate response to the normative and epistemic challenges posed by medical AI.

title: Infrastructural AI and the Redistribution of Agency in Writing Pedagogy
abstract: This article examines how the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into writing instruction redistributes agency across students, tools, instructors, and institutional systems. Rather than treating AI as an external aid or a discrete instance of automation, the article frames contemporary language models as infrastructural technologies that condition the space of possible utterances before writers make conscious choices. Drawing on rhetoric and composition studies, philosophy of technology, and classroom-based observation, it argues that many current pedagogical debates mischaracterize the problem as one of authorship loss or detection, when the more consequential shift concerns responsibility, interpretive transparency, and decision-making within human–machine assemblages. The article proposes an analytic orientation for documenting how agency concentrates, diffuses, or cools across writing processes under conditions of persistent AI use, and suggests pedagogical practices that foreground reflection, traceability, and accountability rather than prohibition or automation. By reframing AI as infrastructure rather than tool or agent, the article offers a pragmatic foundation for teaching writing in environments where human judgment remains essential but no longer operates alone.

title: AI Astrology
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming not only empirical sciences and engineering but also symbolic and interpretive disciplines—fields once thought immune to automation. Over the past decade, the integration of AI into psychology, linguistics, and creativity has blurred the line between rational computation and symbolic meaning. Astrology, traditionally viewed as a symbolic language of consciousness, is undergoing a parallel evolution. The emergence of AI Astrology represents a new phase of this evolution: the use of intelligent algorithms to interpret, model, and dialogue with the archetypal structures encoded in birth charts.

title: The Tranaistor Moment: A Paradigm Beyond the Vacuum Tube Epoch of AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence today remains fundamentally anchored to architectures inherited from classical computing—processing cores, memory banks, and interconnects designed for symbolic, deterministic machines. Akin to the vacuum-tube era of early electronics, AI systems achieve remarkable performance but within an inherited technological substrate -- optimizing within a paradigm whose fundamental assumptions remain unexamined. I propose that transformative breakthroughs emerge not from incremental improvement but from the removal of invisible constraints -- the most transformative phase of AI will not arise from scaling current architectures, but from discovering AI's equivalent of the transistor. An analysis of the gap between biological and artificial computation identifies four architectural blind spots in current AI systems -- structural, functional, phenomenological and relational -- and sketches the contours of what a true paradigm shift might require. AI's future may lie not in bigger models but in a shift towards architectures that embed cognition, context, embodiment, meaning, and relational dynamics as primary, not derived features. This perspective outlines conceptual foundations for the search for AI's first intrinsic technological substrate. The implications extend beyond AI to questions of how technological substrates shape—and limit—human imagination itself.

title: Human-Centered AI in Learning Design: Integrating AI to Support Learners at the Margins
abstract: This paper discusses how human-centered Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be incorporated in the learning design to support education among learners at the periphery, such as low-income earners, low-ethnic minority and disabled learners. The aim of the study is to review how AI-driven technologies can be created and applied to foster equity and inclusion in education. The study uses a mixed-methodology, which involves a combination of both quantitative and qualitative data; pre-intervention and post-intervention assessments, outcomes and qualitative data gathered through interviews and focus groups. The main results show that personalization with AI increases the learning results of marginalized learners by 25 percent on average and raises issues of accessibility and bias. Finally, the field of human-focused AI has a massive potential to close the education disparity, although it needs constant ethical monitoring to guarantee the fair use of its benefits.

title: Creative Writing and AI: A 2024 Case Study
abstract: Abstract This paper analyzes the 2024 Mellichamp Mind and Machine Initiative at UCSB, a pioneering AI-inclusive literary competition accepting human, AI, and hybrid works. As Head Judge, I explore key questions confronting the panel: Will AI render human writing obsolete? Can machine-generated literature exhibit creativity or remain mechanical? Are AI and human writing distinguishable? What does authorship mean in an era of AI collaboration? The paper examines judges’ interpretive frameworks, biases, and expectations, contrasting them with outcomes observed in submissions. It also considers how AI challenges traditional notions of the author and fosters new creative possibilities.

title: Are We There Yet? Notes Towards Benchmarking an Experimental AI-Assisted Workflow for Humanities Data Cleaning and Reconciliation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel AI-assisted pipeline developed to prepare data for the European Research Council-funded project “STEMMA: Systems of Transmitting Early Modern Manuscript Verse, 1475–1700.” Now approaching its midpoint, STEMMA develops and applies a data-driven approach to provide the first comprehensive study of the circulation of early modern English poetry in manuscript. The project began by aggregating and reconciling five of the largest and most authoritative existing datasets about early modern verse circulation. The sheer volume of data, along with the need to preserve early modern English spelling and scribal idiosyncrasies for later analyses, meant that off-the-shelf data cleaning tools like OpenRefine were not fit for purpose. To that end, our software developer created a staged pipeline to aid the removal of duplicates, creation of authorities, reconciliation, and assignment of unique identifiers. The rapid and pragmatic way that this process was developed and deployed means that we did not take the time to benchmark it, nor is it feasible to do so retrospectively. However, this discussion paper records observations from this process and reflects on challenges and bottlenecks as well as opportunities. It points the way toward future benchmarks that are increasingly needed for novel applications of computational methods in the digital humanities. It also briefly considers the relationship between technical benchmarking and research project management.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integrated Communication in Indian Healthcare
Holy AI? Unveiling Magical Images via Photogrammetry
abstract: Recent text-to-image AI systems have revived the long-standing fantasy of the image that appears to generate itself. Building on Chesher and Albarrán-Torres’s concept of ‘autolography’, this article situates contemporary AI-generated imagery within a longer lineage of self-generating images that extends from religious acheiropoieta (‘not made by hand’) through photography to computational image-making. Through the lens of Practice-as-Research (PaR), it positions digital photogrammetry as a knowledge ground in which the fantasy of the self-generating image continues to perform the faith structures of earlier visual cultures. Drawing on photogrammetric experiments originating within Lisbon’s Church of São Domingos in 2018, this article examines unexpected artifacts—ghosts, smears, and fragmentations—that emerge from movement, and reveal the body of the researcher in the centre. It argues that such digital ‘miracle’ images function as contingent, embodied events, and renders visible the labour, presence, and gestures typically erased by automated systems. It playfully proposes the ‘cheiropoieton’ (‘made by hand’) as an embodied counter-ethics to autolography, insisting on friction, care, and accountability in contemporary image-making.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF AN AI LITERACY ASSESSMENT TOOL FOR HIGHER EDUCATION FACULTY IN CHINA: INSIGHTS FROM UNESCO’S AI-CFT FRAMEWORK
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms education globally, assessing teacher AI literacy has become critical—particularly in large-scale, policy-driven systems like China’s. This study develops and validates a contextually grounded assessment instrument for higher education faculty in China, based on UNESCO’s Artificial Intelligence Competency Framework for Teachers (AI-CFT). Through a two-phase validation process—including pilot testing (N = 40) and scale refinement via item analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), and reliability testing—the initial 30-item pool was reduced to a 21-item scale that faithfully reflects the framework’s five dimensions and three proficiency levels. The final instrument demonstrates strong internal consistency (α=0.914) and coherent factor structure, offering a psychometrically sound tool for evaluating AI literacy in non-Western, high-digitalization educational contexts. This work not only advances the cross-cultural operationalization of UNESCO’s AI-CFT but also provides a validated foundation for teacher development, policy implementation, and comparative research on AI readiness in higher education.

title: AI Revolution: Redefining Content Creation in the Digital Age
abstract: Generative models have revolutionized content creation in the text, image, video, audio, and 3D domains. This is arguably the most significant milestone in artificial intelligence to date concerning its impact on society. ChatGPT, DALL-E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion are already at industrial maturity with broad adoption and have started to change professional practices within journalism, marketing, education, entertainment as well as law. These systems use high-level natural language understanding capabilities together with state-of-the-art machine learning techniques to create new content that is human-like and this has never been achieved before. At the same time that such technological advancement has taken place there are very critical challenges that need immediate attention. Issues regarding authorship, originality as well as protection of intellectual property are still debated; socio-political biases that are embedded within the systems pose risks of misinformation which can threaten societal trust Embedded biases and misinformation risks threaten societal trust. There is a performance gap between what users expect from these systems and what they can actually deliver: this reveals some basic limitations in understanding and quality of generation. More than just technical challenges ,the growing use of generative AI calls for strong accountability ,transparency and governance frameworks . Workflows are being reorganized professionally requiring new quality standards and models for collaboration ,while economic disruption threatens traditional creative sectors . This paper looks at these different sides on short ,medium and long-term horizons judging both commercial paths as well as those taken by open-source projects . It describes how AI-driven creation of content is currently happening with some potential to change things radically but also real risks attached .Gains from generative AI will not be fully reaped unless ethical guidelines regulatory frameworks safety benchmarks plus knowledge sharing mechanisms involving all stakeholders develop together Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Age, Journalism, Education, Communication

title: Analysis on the epidemiological characteristics and prevention and control strategies of drinking tea-type endemic fluorosis in Xizang
abstract: Drinking tea-type endemic fluorosis is a type of fluorosis caused by the long-term consumption of tea with excessive fluoride content. Due to Xizang’s unique natural environment and special socio-cultural background， this disease is particularly prevalent in the region. Patients with drinking tea-type endemic fluorosis typically exhibit varying degrees of dental fluorosis and skeletal fluorosis， with the severity of the disease influenced by factors such as age， region， and the amount of brick tea consumed by residents. This paper systematically reviews relevant literature， summarizing the prevalence of drinking tea-type endemic fluorosis in Xizang from 1983 to 2020 and disease prevention strategies from 2015 to 2025. It explores the discovery process， geographical distribution characteristics， comparative analysis of different types of fluorosis， differences compared to fluorosis in other regions， and factors influencing the prevalence rate in Xizang. The aim is to provide a scientific basis and reference for further research and control of drinking tea-type endemic fluorosis in Xizang.

title: Data mining and risk characterization of chlorate exposure in infant formula based on literature from 2019 to 2024
abstract: ObjectiveUtilizing literature data mining， this study analyzed the exposure risk of chlorate in infant formula for Chinese infants， providing scientific evidence for the risk management of chlorate in infant formula.MethodsBased on chlorate levels in infant formula reported in publicly available literature from 2019 to 2024， combined with consumption patterns of infant formula in China， a simple distribution assessment method was used to evaluate chronic exposure risk in infants aged 0-36 months.ResultsLiterature data indicate that chlorate concentrations in infant formula sampled from distribution channels in China ranged from non-detectable to 3 250.00 µg/kg， with a mean concentration of 99.14 µg/kg. The chronic exposure assessment indicated that both the mean exposure level ［0.73 µg/（kg·BW）］ and the P95 exposure level ［1.86 µg/（kg·BW）］ among infant consumers were below the Provisional Maximum Tolerable Daily Intake （PMTDI） of 10 µg/（kg·BW） for chlorate established by the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives （JECFA）.ConclusionBased on data mining and analysis of literature published from 2019 to 2024， the overall risk of chlorate exposure among Chinese infant consumers is relatively low.

title: Organic Growing Media from Tea Waste for Orchids in Kalimantan
abstract: This study investigates the potential of using organic media derived from tea waste and young coconut water for the cultivation of Epidendrum orchids, a rare species native to Kalimantan, Indonesia. The research aims to replace conventional instant tissue culture media (ICM), which contains hazardous chemicals, with environmentally friendly alternatives. The organic media (OM) formulations were prepared by fermenting tea waste to extract nutrients and combining them with coconut water, which is rich in growth hormones. The effectiveness of three different organic media compositions (OM-1 [50ml Compost Extract], OM-2 [100ml Compost Extract], OM-3 [150ml Compost Extract]) was evaluated based on their nutrient content and impact on the growth of orchid explants. Results indicated that the organic media provided sufficient nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels, leading to a 100% survival rate of the explants. Notably, OM-1 demonstrated the highest stem growth (0.46%) and shoot proliferation (2.3) compared to other treatments. This research highlights the feasibility of utilizing organic waste for sustainable orchid cultivation, reducing hazardous waste production, and promoting environmental conservation. Keywords: Environment sustainability, hazardous chemicals, plant tissue culture, organic matter, sustainable cultivation.

title: Assessing opportunities for organic tomato farming: a PESTEL perspective on sustainable agriculture
abstract: PESTEL research determines organic tomato farming chances in North Sulawesi Province, Indonesia. This mixed-method study interviews 100 consumers and 20 farmers. This study indicates that environmental and social awareness increases the organic tomato market's capacity to improve agricultural sustainability. Market access and farmer yields will improve with government help, public knowledge, and technical advancement. Thus, many organic farmers can balance yields and incomes. Disastrous weather, pests, and diseases are hurdles. Farmers with organic certification earn more and produce more sustainably. This report stresses the necessity for concerted efforts to overcome historical limitations and improve organic tomato production. Government, farmers, and research organizations must collaborate to enhance agricultural practices and yields. Knowledge of the sector's external environment can help stakeholders improve sustainable agricultural policies and initiatives. This study advances organic farming science and helps the agriculture industry's future. This study supports an eco-friendly approach that meets customer and market needs. This study can help policymakers and practitioners improve contemporary, ecological agriculture worldwide. Keywords: Organic agriculture, climate change, vegetable cultivation, environmental sustainability, consumer awareness, agricultural policy.

title: Chitosan-Based Coatings for Fruit Preservation: A Bibliometric Study and Evidence of Shelf-Life Extension
abstract: Post-harvest fruit losses threaten food security. We conducted a PRISMA-guided bibliometric mapping and descriptive synthesis of shelf-life outcomes. A Scopus search on 10 June 2025 (original research, English, final versions) yielded 1,087 articles (1993–2025). Two reviewers screened titles/abstracts and full texts. Scientific mapping (Bibliometrix, VOSviewer) shows output rising since 2017, with the latest period (2017–2025) contributing 864/1,087 records (~79%) and 21,891 citations. China leads production and international collaboration. Research concentrates on strawberry, mango, tomato, grape and papaya. Shelf life was harmonised to days; within each study we extracted paired values for chitosan-treated fruit and its matched control under identical storage. Illustrative pairs show Citrus × sinensis 30.9 vs 17.5 days, Pyrus communis 21.4 vs 7.0, and Vaccinium spp. 14.8 vs 5.7. Formulations with essential oils (n=90) and metallic nanoparticles (n=89) were the most frequently investigated and were often associated with longer shelf life and antifungal/antioxidant effects in individual studies. Overall, chitosan coatings emerge as a bio-based, biodegradable and widely investigated approach to mitigating post-harvest losses. Keywords: Biocontrol; chitosan; antifungal; food loss mitigation; fruit.

title: La politique et la morale chez Montaigne et Pascal : le respect de la loi, même injuste, et l’aversion pour la réforme politique
abstract: Politics and Morality in Montaigne and Pascal : Respect for the Law, Even When Unjust, and Aversion to Political Reform. We propose a comparative study of the political thought of Montaigne and Pascal, focusing on their shared insistence on respect for the law, even when it is unjust, and on their common distrust of political reform. An examination of textual parallels between the Essays and the Pensées highlights Pascal’s appropriation of Montaigne’s idea that laws derive their authority not from justice but from custom and usage. At the same time, it brings out Pascal’s own inflections, notably his emphasis on the role of imagination and on the political dangers involved in exposing the arbitrariness of laws. Finally, the convergence of the two authors in their aversion to political innovation is related to a theological justification of Augustinian inspiration, which subordinates political action to the preservation of civil peace.

title: Pascal et Roberval : collaboration par intermittences, indifférence savante et joie dans la découverte mathématique
abstract: This work focuses on what is known about the relationship between Pascal and Roberval and a scientific collaboration that was intermittent, but particularly intense during the year 1658, in which the method of indivisibles underwent a radical transformation. The following year it culminated in the Lettres de A. Dettonville in which Roberval finally appears as a witness among a few rare others including Huygens, certainly far from the officially shown indifference to the advances about the cycloid of a John Wallis who highlighted Christopher Wren. Since Roberval had a personal experience of a struggle with a devotee of indivisibles like Torricelli less than twenty years earlier, and was aware of living with Pascal at a time conducive to mathematical innovation, I seek in these short years, which are also the writing of the Pensées, to uncover how both an indifference to results that are fundamentally technical and a joy in mathematical discovery are manifested. Perhaps because this joy was shared by a small, if not friendly, at least convivial community in active solidarity for the sake of progress, which will be described as forming the basis of the future Academies of Sciences.

title: Sur les Provinciales et la querelle des rites
abstract: This contribution attempts to articulate two aspects of Pascal's thought that are generally perceived as being very far apart: on the one hand, his criticism of the practices of accommodatio (or adaptation to ritual contexts) in modern evangelization, particularly in China; on the other hand, his criticism of probabilism in the context of controversies over casuistry. On the one hand, therefore, the apostolate; on the other, moral theology. On the one hand, Asia; on the other, Europe. However, in the extremely tense context of the Holy See's challenge to accommodatio in the second half of the 17th century, we discover a short circuit in a little-read passage of the fifth Provincial Letter between, on the one hand, the Jesuit defense of the adoption of Confucian rites and, on the other, the use of probability in the development of these lines of defense, precisely identified and criticized by the author of the Provincial Letters. This short circuit of a few lines actually opens up the possibility of a set of new connections between theory and practice, between the West and the East, and between the work of the Messieurs de Port-Royal on the Society of Jesus (Arnauld in particular) and Pascal himself.

title: Bourdieu et Pascal. Penser avec, ou Comment métaboliser un auteur ?
abstract: This article argues that Pierre Bourdieu’s Pascalian Meditations does not so much offer a commentary on Pascal as present a mode of thinking with him through the metabolization of his thought. What initially appears is an author-to-author relationship that presents itself as unmediated, notably remaining silent about its most plausible Marxist intermediaries (from Lefebvre to Goldmann). More fundamentally, however, Pascalian Meditations enacts a sociological actualization of Pascal, visible in the intertextual dialogue produced through Bourdieu’s notably loose practice of quotation, allusion, and reformulation. Pascal thus emerges as a tool for critical and reflexive inquiry, as a model for a praxeological approach capable of moving beyond the entrenched oppositions between objectivism and subjectivism, determinism and freedom. Bourdieu’s engagement with Pascal aims to promote the principle of the non-excluded middle, set against both the structuralist theory of rules and, by extension, “the Marxist vision of the centralized apparatus” and of mechanical alienation. Neither philological nor doctrinal, and characterized by processes of displacement and fluid absorption, Bourdieu’s claimed fidelity to Pascal is primarily pragmatic: it serves a struggle that is at once political and methodological—less as a means of asserting a position than as a means of clarification, understood here as a release from any overly simplistic framework.

title: L’anomalie chez Pascal
abstract: In this powerful article, with his characteristic precise and penetrating style, our late friend constructs a concept of anomaly as “a significant irregularity behind apparent regularity,” which “persists in every ecosystem, [...] even those of the mind.” Echoing Pascal with references drawn mainly from the Bible and ecclesiastical history, but also from Durkheim, Livy, Nietzsche, and Döblin, he reveals anomaly (and the closely related concepts of syncope, aporia, and anomie) as the structuring principle of his writings, primarily the Pensées. Arguing for a more oral reading of the Pensées, he highlights a constitutive anomaly in their style, their syncopated rhythm, rich in destabilizing effects and significant irregularities. He emphasizes the relationship between this discursive practice and the Christocentrism of the Pensées, where Christ appears as a ‘living anomaly, an incarnate anomaly.’

title: La Société des « Amis de Pascal » (1923-1930)
abstract: The Society of the ‘Friends of Pascal’ (1923-1930). On 19 June 1923, the Catholic Church commemorated the birth of Blaise Pascal, ‘whose genius is one of the glories of France and of the Church’. Following this event, The Reverend Jean-Amable de La Valette-Monbrun created an association of ‘Friends of Pascal’ to ‘promote the study of Pascalian thought’ through conferences and a periodical.The bimonthly journal Conversations of the ‘Friends of Pascal’ continued the celebration of ‘the great evangelist’ until 1930 with contributions from an ‘elite of intellectuals’. The twenty-four issues of the Conversations, totalling almost one thousand two hundred pages, reflect various interpretations of Pascal at the time of his third centenary. They shed new light on the intellectual, political and ecclesiastical controversies of the 1920s.

title: La consécration de Pascal-écrivain national en 1923 ou la création d’un devoir de mémoire
abstract: Pascal was celebrated very early on as one of the greatest writers of his generation and, from the end of the 18th century, as the “créateur” or “fixateur” of the French language. However, it was not until the 300th anniversary of his birth (1923) that this glory took on an official dimension. Why did celebrations of Pascal begin in 1923? To shed light on this cultural enigma, the article examines the discourses and practices celebrating him as a national writer. The analysis focuses on three contextual elements: the rise of literary nationalism, of a proto-fascism hostile to science and rationalism, and of a “moral crisis” during the early 20th century.

title: Pascal et l’« homme de notre temps » (Royaumont, 1954-1956)
abstract: This article focuses on an event from a relatively recent epoch in Blaise Pascal's history. A decade after the Second World War, a few months after Stalin's death, a celebration was organized at Royaumont to mark the tercentenary of Pascal's Memorial. This event, modeled on those held at Pontigny in previous decades, fostered lively and courteous exchanges about the relationship between various forms of Christianism and Marxism. Pascal served as a tool for the participants to define "the man of [their] time," but Royaumont could not offer them a sufficiently utopian place so that the Pensées can unleash the power of neutralizing opposites which is deeply inscribed within them, and reveal the possibility of a new kind of human being.

title: La haie et la plaie : Lire les Pensées de Pascal aujourd’hui
abstract: “The Hedge and the Wound: Reading Pascal’s Pensées Today” - This article examines the conditions and difficulties involved in reading Pascal’s Pensées today. The title “La Haie et la Plaie” (The Hedge and the Wound) refers to two structuring images: the hedge, which designates the growing obstacle created by so‑called “objective” editions and by modern philological apparatuses – an obstacle which, while clarifying the organization of the manuscript, paradoxically renders the work less accessible; and the wound, which instead designates the radical openness of Pascalian thinking, its constitutive vulnerability, and the exposure of the text to incompleteness, chance, and loss.By retracing the editorial history of the Pensées and the contrasting positions of contemporary readers – from the theologian who seeks their apologetic utility, from the philologist who reconstructs the presumed order of the Apology, from the reader who is content with a circumstantial meaning and prefers a readable textus receptus over an origin judged inaccessible, to those who advocate a reading freed from any overarching intent – the article shows that modern reading unfolds within the tension between these poles.Its main contribution is to offer a reflection on the very possibility of reading Pascal today, proposing to move beyond the scholarly enclosure of the “hedge” through renewed attention to “the wound of thinking”: openness, fragility, and incompleteness understood as sites of philosophical experience rather than defects to be overcome. This perspective invites a form of seriousness that proceeds through hermeneutics rather than philology, thereby allowing one to remain with Pascal “on this side of apology,” where hedge and wound meet.
publisher: Groupe de Recherches Interdisciplinaires sur l'Histoire du Littéraire
concepts: Social history and conditions. Social problems. Social reform

title: Expérience, écriture, transmission. Les pratiques de Florin Périer, beau-frère de Blaise Pascal
abstract: This article analyses the central role of the Périer family in the creation, writing and transmission of “Pascal”, focusing in particular on the practices of Florin Périer, his brother-in-law. Returning to the critical concept of “family tradition” used by Jean Mesnard, it highlights the historiographical erasure of the Périer family’s own practices of writing and experimentation in favour of the construction of Pascal’s work. Drawing on a detailed study of editorial mechanisms, manuscript and printed writings, and the physical acts of preserving and repeating the scientific experiments conducted by Florin Périer at Blaise’s request, the article demonstrates how kinship functioned very early on as a social framework for Pascal’s scholarly authorship, within which Florin Périer developed his own practices of experimentation and publication. Based on the example of a ‘family of letters’, the aim is to present the family as a context in its own right, operating according to its own logic, within scientific and literary activity.

concepts: Social history and conditions. Social problems. Social reform

title: Exemplaire Pascal
abstract: The famous pensée on examples (Sellier 454) usually puzzles the reader with the false symmetry of these propositions: “When one wishes to demonstrate a general principle, one must provide the specific rule for a particular case. But if one wishes to demonstrate a particular case, one must begin with the specific rule.” To take seriously the injunction “begin with the specific rule,” instead of the “general rule,” which is expected—taking it seriously even if one reads it as a lapsus, that error which by definition carries the weight of a symptom—and doing so, in particular, by placing this pensée within its page context, allows us to understand that the theory of examples in the Pensées moves away from Aristotle and profoundly alters classical theories of exemplarity. For Pascal, there is no ready-made general principle waiting for us somewhere, no natural foundation, no law that is just in itself. Thus, to prove the validity of a principle amidst the particularity of cases, one must construct regularity within a dynamic of the clear and the opaque. The apologist must find the most rightful operators of an exemplification that never entirely erases the traces of the actions and the actors who carried it out.
publisher: Groupe de Recherches Interdisciplinaires sur l'Histoire du Littéraire

title: Une « philosophie de la priorité » : l’évaluation de la validité des solutions mathématiques dans le concours sur la roulette lancé par Blaise Pascal en 1658
abstract: Blaise Pascal addressed the question of generality in mathematics within a very specific context: the mathematical competition on the Cycloid (or Roulette), which he launched anonymously in 1658. After judging the answers submitted to the competition (primarily by Father Antoine de Lalouvère and John Wallis), he himself proposed a solution using a “general method for centres of gravity,” signed with the pseudonym A. Dettonville. Here, we examine the criteria established by Pascal for considering an answer to the competition as a valid solution, from the point of view of its “generality.” To do so, we revisit the historical context of the competition by analysing Pascal’s three “letters” (or “writings”) that define its conditions, in order to assess his “philosophy of priority”—an expression we borrow from Pierre Costabel to designate more broadly the criteria present in all the conditions that Pascal set for the competition.

title: La Nōson Seinen Sha, commune anarchiste dans le Japon impérial : théoriser et vivre la révolution (1931)
abstract: Anarchism and Japan: for many, these two terms form a diametrically opposed couple. Indeed, well-entrenched stereotypes, often racist or at least strongly orientalist, frequently describe Japan as the very example of an authoritarian society, disciplined and subject to authority, even fond of authority, making little use of individual freedoms and in which, according to the proverb, "you have to drive in the nail that sticks out" (deru kugi wa utareru). Such clichés, however, obscure the long history of anarchism in Japan and its considerable influence on Japanese society. Anarcho-communist approaches, debates and groups, with their concrete ideas and experiences of community life in the 1920s and 1930s, such as that of the Nōson Seinen Sha, are one example among many of the historical diversity and influence of anarchist thought and action in this country. It is both a form of protest, but also, in a certain way, a real revolution that highlights this aspect of Japanese history, as well as a place where a whole series of theoretical considerations have emerged, practical implementations and socio-political conflicts. This article deals with the anarchist community of the Nōson Seinen Sha and considers its self-management and self-sufficiency practices in the interwar period as a criticism, practice and expression of anti-state, anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist protest.

La nation et les classes sociales dans l’« Histoire en construction » de Pierre Vilar
abstract: The article presents the work of Pierre Vilar (1906-2003), historian and defender of history, as a profession and scientific discipline but also, of course, subject of problematic reflections. Following the analytical and theoretical tools of Marxism, his research/discoveries as a geographer and field historian have influenced many historians around the world, especially in the Iberian and Latin American worlds. Encouraging total history and the practice of thinking historically from the historical analysis of socioeconomic structures, its approach to the historical category "nation" from his research on modern and contemporary Catalonia allows to immerse oneself in the dialectic between social classes and national fact. Twenty-three years after his death, it is time to remember his legacy, a true "Vilarian work" to be known.

title: De la réalité historique au mythe : la Festa di a Nazione corse
abstract: In Corsica, today, December 8 takes on a particular character, going beyond the simple religious framework (feast of the Immaculate Conception) to embrace a more identity and political aspect. Indeed, the island nationalist movement solemnly associates it with A Festa di a Nazione – The Nation’s Day -, which recalls that the island, in the 18th century, in rebellion against Genoa (from 1729), would have was placed under the protection of the Virgin on January 30, 1735, during a Cunsulta – Assembly – which took place in Corte. However, the date of January 30 is debated among some historians, as to its authenticity and the proclamation of December 8 as the Corsican Nation’s Day. This controversy is also fueled by the existence of another date, that of November 30, 1789, namely the accession of Corsica to the French Imperium – Empire – and to the principles of the Revolution. The significance of this event is further reinforced by the decision taken by the Assembly – Cunsulta – of Orezza, on September 23, 1790, to make November 30 the National Day of Corsica. Through these two dates, two conceptions of history appear in counterpoint: that of the national novel and that of historical authenticity.
concepts: Consulte of Orezza ; Pascal Paoli ; Corsica ; Riacquistu

title: Tout sur Marie
L’histoire du football : populaire, forcément populaire ?
abstract: The notion of people’s history requires defining the “people” being referred to when dealing with football, even though this sport initially spread through channels close to the elites. While it now occupies a dominant position in popular tastes, it could still appear, as Alfred Wahl wrote, “too commonly popular” to be taken seriously, including by the proponents of history bearing that very name. Consequently, people’s history in general, and that of football in particular, cannot avoid requiring the historian to reflect on the author, the intended audience, and the media through which it is written.

title: Pour une histoire populaire des techniques : matérialité, innovations et usages à l’âge industriel
abstract: Technical equipment and infrastructure have long remained outside of so-called popular history, except through the rise of consumerism, initially perceived as a prerequisite for emancipation and social progress. But at a time when digital giants are triumphing, a new authoritarian technopolitics and unbridled consumerism are on the rise, and whereas we need to reimagine other technical and material worlds adapted to the reality of planetary limits, it is urgent and necessary to break with the dominant teleological narratives and rediscover the richness of the popular history of technology.

title: Réflexions sur l’histoire populaire
abstract: This article reflects on the evolution, erosion, and contemporary necessity of people’s history as both a method and a political project. Emerging alongside modern historiography in the wake of the French Revolution, people’s history originally sought to centre the labouring classes, recover marginalised voices, and analyse society through the Marxist framework of class struggle. Foundational historians such as Michelet, Bloch, Thompson, Habib, and Rudé demonstrated that understanding social change requires attention to the lived experiences and contradictions shaping workers’ and peasants’ lives. From the late twentieth century onward, however, the rise of post-structuralism, cultural history, and post-Marxist thought shifted scholarship toward fragmented identities and away from class analysis, weakening the holistic, emancipatory ambitions of earlier “history from below.” The article also examines the growing divide between academic historiography and public engagement, driven by university privatisation, professionalisation, and the enclosure of knowledge behind paywalls. Against this backdrop, it argues for a renewed, politically committed history for the people—a practice rooted in mass education, collective intellectual life, and the battle of ideas. Drawing on the work of Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, it calls for rebuilding democratic historical consciousness as a foundation for contemporary struggles against capitalism, colonialism, and the far right.
concepts: People’s history ; history from below ; Class struggle ; Marxist historiography ; Post-structuralism ; historiographical fragmentation ; Public history ; political education ; Tricontinental

title: Histoire populaire et popularisation de la science : le prix Unesco Kalinga de vulgarisation scientifique
abstract: Since its foundation in 1945, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has created more than 25 highly diverse prizes, all intended to reward and promote original contributions to peace through culture. Among them, the oldest—established in 1950–51—is the Kalinga Prize for the Popularization of Science. Created at the initiative of an Indian philanthropist, only three years after India’s independence and at a time when this great country was rising on the international stage, notably as a Third World nations and then a non-aligned nation, how does this prize clearly illustrate UNESCO’s aspiration to contribute to social and human progress through the promotion of science and rational thinking within society? And how has it evolved over time up to the present day, shifting from a prize that was initially elitist, male-dominated, and Europe-centered to one more open to women, to peoples of the Global South, and to mass mediation aimed at the widest possible public?

title: Introduction. Pour l’histoire populaire !
Une histoire du peuple pour le peuple ?
abstract: What means people in a people’s history? If it is used to describe history seen from below, we can also consider that people refer to the readership for which this history is intended. In other words, how can we write history for a widest possible audience when the social space is saturated with the conservative vision of the national narrative, now subsidised by far-right patrons? This article examines the writing of a people’s history that avoids both the pitfalls of falsehoods and the chauvinistic trap that would lock the country France into an eternal past. In doing so, we approach the question of the people’s history from the perspective of popular education. The challenge is to show the emancipatory nature of a people’s history.
concepts: people’s history ; national narrative ; historical popularisation ; emancipation
